Architecture.name: SHEETH
Architecture.description: SHEETH. A Blueprint for Building Relationships. Built Right. Together. Lasting relationships are a tough thing to build in construction. The stakes are high, the pressure even higher, and clients want to be certain they can trust the builders whose shoulders their vision (quite literally) rests on. Against this challenging backdrop, SHEETH wanted to forge partnerships with more developers, architects and business owners all over Australia. And to build those relationships, they needed to build a new brand. Sectors: Construction, Architecture. Services: Brand Positioning, Brand Territory, Visual Identity, Brand Essence, Tone of Voice, Brand Guidelines, UX/UI, Web Design, Prototyping, Stationery, Big Idea, Merchandising, Brand Strategy. Challenge: So, what are clients looking for in a new builder? What qualities seal the deal, and which ones break it? Throughout our client interviews, industry trend research and in-depth discovery calls, the same criteria came up time and time again: Clients don't just want technical mastery, they want good old-fashioned empathy. Safety and quality are essential expectations, but if their partner doesn't put as much effort into the relationship as the structure itself, it won't be a pleasant experience overall. From start to finish, they want someone who's responsive, approachable and, crucially, keeps their cool when latent issues (inevitably) rear their head. No egos, no finger-pointing, no dramas. Until they see that kind of emotional intelligence, they won't switch to someone new. Solution: To earn clients' trust, SHEETH needed to show up differently. We positioned them as the firm that brings both excellence and engagement to every partnership. Drawing inspiration from the satisfying symmetry of their name, we developed the Double E Experience, a methodology demonstrating how they deliver precision and collaboration at every project stage, from early coordination to post-completion. This double DNA formed the core pillars of the new brand, supporting every layer of their new look, feel and messaging. Their imagery captured their meticulous processes and moments of human connection alike; the tone of voice channelled the dual personality of the "engineer next door"; and the iconography featured a series of interlocking cinder blocks, a beautifully reassuring metaphor for SHEETH's rock-solid partnerships. The takeaway from all this? In an industry that offers an abundance of expertise, empathy is the most vital material.

Architecture.name: Sekisui House
Architecture.description: Sekisui House — Advancing Sekisui House's brand impact within Australia. Here for better. Since 2016, TOAST has partnered with global property leader Sekisui House, the world's largest residential developer and a benchmark for sustainable living. What began as a single engagement has grown into a long-term collaboration built on shared ambition, integrity and an obsession with craft. Together, we've helped redefine how a property brand can look, feel and behave in the Australian market. Challenge: Sekisui House's legacy of innovation is unmatched globally, yet in Australia the brand needed a refreshed, connected experience—one that translated its philosophy of better living into a contemporary, local context. The task was to bring clarity, cohesion and emotional resonance to a brand operating in a competitive and rapidly shifting property landscape, while honouring its deep design principles and human-centred values. Solution: TOAST worked side-by-side with Sekisui House to elevate every touchpoint of its brand experience—uniting strategy, design and storytelling into a single, purposeful narrative. This collaborative foundation ultimately led to TOAST being entrusted with full branding and marketing responsibilities for Sekisui House Australia's two newest Sydney communities in Norwest and Wentworth Point. The result is a partnership that continues to shape how Australians engage with place: thoughtful, detailed, quietly bold—and always moving toward what's next.

Architecture.name: Arclane
Architecture.description: Arclane — Brand Transformation. Makers of Modern Living. Standing Out by Standing for Artistry. Arclane are an ultra-creative, premium property developer. Like any ambitious business at the height of their craft, they were looking to strengthen their presence in the Australian property market. And they didn't just want an immediate impact or a quick win: they wanted to build a brand that would nurture steady growth for years to come. Challenge: Cutting through in the world of property is a tall order. It's a market with big players and considerable competition, each striving to be top of mind for buyers, architects and investors alike, so it's very easy to be crowded out and become invisible. But while there's no shortage of developers, there is a gap in the market: there are many formulaic, standard-issue developments out there. They tick the boxes and make commercial sense, but lack the sense of flair or beauty that make them a truly high-value property. But Arclane is different. Following a series of in-depth strategic interviews with their team, we discovered their unique value in the market: They approach every space with the care and consideration of a craftsperson, blending aesthetics and functionality to create spaces that are as beautiful as they are usable. They're places that inspire and you can admire, while still having the right features to support living, working and playing with ease. Instead of being places people just spend time in or move through, they're places people love. Solution: This insight led to our brand idea, "Makers of Modern Living". It captures how every development perfectly marries form and function, beauty and purpose, to provide a refined and modern living experience. By giving residents the best of both worlds, and standing for something more aspirational than transactional, it was a real challenge to the status quo of the market. It was then a question of applying this philosophy to everything the brand made, said and did. We created a design system that was spacious, clean and easily navigable, but with plenty of flourishes mixed in: flowing lines, elegant curves and elevated imagery, all the finishing touches that make you stop and stare. The logo then brought it all together in a symbol of incredible visual economy. "Makers of Modern Living" was etched into its very shape, with three arched versions of the letter "M" combining to create a stunning building. A true work of art, just like their developments. The Results: "Makers of Modern Living" proved to be the perfect platform for the brand. Not only is the idea distinctive in the market, it elegantly summarises what makes Arclane's developments of superior value. Which just goes to show: to avoid becoming invisible, you need to lean into your beauty.

Architecture.name: Altis
Architecture.description: Altis. Brand Transformation. Work That Works. Altis is an architectural firm based in Sydney. Through combining both architecture and interior design principles, Altis creates gathering places that people love, and where businesses thrive; the driving force behind their business being to create unique hospitality, club and living destinations that communities embrace. They are passionate about helping hospitality and living businesses excel and enhance the lives of the people in their local communities. Altis expertly delivers multi-disciplined business solutions by integrating architecture, interior design, strategy and deep local immersion. However, this passion and expertise was not evidenced in their brand territory. Their actions were progressing beyond the public face of their brand, which needed to change. Challenge: Our team was presented with the challenge of refreshing and elevating the Altis brand to reflect their market-leading stature and growing reputation in the architecture and design realm. At TOAST, we attest that a brand governs how you make an impact on the world. It leaves lasting memories on the people who interact with it. For Altis, our task was thus to cleanly define and effectively articulate their proposition. This involved increasing the understanding of the firm's expertise and projects and boosting awareness of the value within their services. Solution: Altis creates strategic solutions in response to diverse business challenges. They transform places into unique destinations by designing elevated experiences for business success. In reaching the core of this branding challenge, our team had to unwind Altis' business strengths and opportunities, delve into similar market leaders and audit their factors of success, all to rearticulate and strengthen the brand footprint and principles of the Altis brand. The fundamental strength our team consistently uncovered was that Altis has a unique business vision that works. Through a tailored approach with holistic integration, their design solutions enable growth and create impact. TOAST captured this transformative service in their new logotype and brand image. The logotype concept builds upon the previous logo's heritage with minimalist, clean-cut design language to capture the precise, technical backbone of the brand. Exuding a considered and crafted feel, the branding combines structural lines with subtle curves that convey Altis' professionalism. Meanwhile, the overlapping colours in the "A" hint at a process of transformation. This concept combines a powerful burgundy with a solid charcoal in a sophisticated palette that can be translated through the brand's marketing collateral. Altis' uplifted brand territory and visual identity has been refined to elevate the experiential luxury and functionality they expertly deliver across major commercial and hospitality projects.

Architecture.name: Xavier Knight
Architecture.description: Xavier Knight. Brand Transformation. Life is Multiplied. Established 10 years ago, engineering consultancy firm Xavier Knight aim to raise the standard of engineering services currently available in our built environment. The company combines the capabilities of a Tier 1 consultancy with a dynamic, proactive approach to collaboration and design. They work on an array of engineering projects, across structural and civil construction engineering through to modern digital engineering in a 3, 4 and 5D scope. Their team and endeavours are constantly expanding. TOAST was engaged to represent this in a brand footprint that is fit for their growing and progressive vision. Challenge: TOAST's challenge was to bring new life to Xavier Knight's brand identity. The brand's positioning had to emphasise their uniquely people-centric, progressive values, whilst reflecting their professionalism and credibility. This positioning would be launched through a 30-second impact video at a UDIA industry event, and further established through collateral including a website, capability statement and tendering document. Solution: TOAST's interview and brand audit process uncovered a clear insight: that Xavier Knight's core purpose was 'to enrich life and the world we live in'. This insight, coupled with the firm's 'X' brandmark, inspired our Big Idea 'Life is Multiplied'. This statement reflects Xavier Knight's intentions to enrich lives and amplify outcomes. This idea was brought to life in an attention-grabbing 30-second impact video, using the 'X' as a multiplication symbol in a series of brand claims. The entire suite of collateral, from website to official documentation, builds upon this idea. A predominantly black and white palette maintains professionalism and consistency with prior brand positioning. However, people-centric imagery, strategic hero messaging and splashes of colour ensure that the brand is given a sense of life and vitality. TOAST has enjoyed creating a brand identity that gives justice to Xavier Knight's unique, people-centric positioning.

Community.name: Solutions +
Community.description: Solutions +. Brand Transformation. We Bring the +. Uniting a World of Services Under One Plus. Solutions Group was a huge collection of specialisms and services. They had one business for turfcare, another for golf courses, another for civil engineering, another for habitat protection... and so on. If you had a construction, maintenance or landscaping issue, chances are they'd be able to fix it. Sectors: Construction, Technology, Community. Services: Brand Architecture, Brand Positioning, Unique Value Proposition, Service Positioning, Brand Territory, Visual Identity, Brand Essence, Tone of Voice, Brand Guidelines, Stationery, Motion Graphics, UX/UI, Web Design. Challenge: They'd grown to the point where they needed an overarching brand to unite these services. This would not only create more belonging and coordination between their teams, but also show clients the full breadth of what they could do, allowing them to cross-sell and grow more easily. But to bring all these services together, we needed to find the thread that ran through every single thing they did - from the boardroom all the way to the teams on the ground. Solution: We audited the business on every level, reviewing their capabilities, interviewing staff and workshopping with team leads, to uncover the group's common values, principles and practices. What we found was a common culture of added value: whether it's mowing grass, laying brickwork or fixing faults, their staff always overdeliver. They don't just get the job done: they go above and beyond what's expected with a range of extra benefits and services - from being on-call whenever you need them and engaging with the local community to flagging risks well before they happen. We made this incredible work ethic the value proposition of the whole group, giving them a new name, Solutions+, a new tagline, "We bring the +", and a visual identity brimming with energy. Then it was a question of re-aligning their brand architecture. Their different business units were all re-designed under the new brand, but each one would now be listed as a sub-service on their website, instead of a separate company. And to make sure visitors could quickly find the right specialism for their needs, we restructured the site with plenty of signposts, a simple UX/UI navigation and a clear user journey from start to finish. Result: With one simple symbol to rally behind, every employee now has a clear idea of what unites the group, allowing the whole business to push in the same direction, with more cohesion, efficiency and coordination on every level. And now that clients can see that Solutions+ is a one-stop shop for all their construction, maintenance and landscaping needs, the group is winning business more seamlessly. A plus for their culture, a plus for their operations and, ultimately, a plus for their profits.

Community.name: FORGE
Community.description: FORGE. Brand Transformation. Unlock the Outdoors. FLEETWOOD BECOMING FORGE. How Strategy is a Key Weapon in Brand Transformation. Fleetwood, a leader in outdoor infrastructure solutions, faced the challenge of evolving into a more dynamic, scalable brand that could attract larger clients, expand its community projects from design to delivery, and increase its market share. Through competitive global benchmarking, national industry research, key stakeholders involvement and cultural assessments, we crafted the 2030 Fleetwood strategic-led solution defining a company's unique DNA and positioning for lasting impact. Sectors: Construction, Corporate, Community. Services: Brand Positioning, Unique Value Proposition, Naming, Brand Territory, Visual Identity, Brand Essence, Tone of Voice, Brand Guidelines, UX/UI, Web Design, Motion Graphics, Video Production. Challenge: How can a well-established business with strong equity reposition itself for greater national impact while retaining its legacy of success? In a fast-changing market, even established brands must evolve to stay competitive. Legacy alone isn't enough and strategic repositioning unlocks new opportunities, strengthening market presence, and driving long-term growth. The challenge was to strategically transition from Fleetwood's existing identity to a stronger, unified national presence; one that encapsulated its ambition, growth mindset, and long-term vision. Solution: Through our rigorous process, we had to extract Fleetwood's core strengths and aspirations, incorporating creative thinking, emotional engagement, and pragmatic execution to establish a new, differentiated brand territory with a compelling name: FORGE. Through our strategic methodology, TOAST helped Fleetwood evolve into FORGE with a comprehensive solution that included: A Unified Brand Vision: Establishing a clear and future-focused brand strategy that strengthens FORGE's leadership in outdoor infrastructure. An Incomparable Selling Weapon: A structured, results-driven methodology that empowers FORGE with a winning approach to pitches, project delivery, and client success. A Compelling and Engaging Tagline: "Unlock The Outdoors"; a brand promise that captures the essence of FORGE's mission to create spaces that inspire and connect. A Strong Brand Visualisation: A distinctive and powerful identity that highlights FORGE's expertise in design thinking, engineering excellence, and flawless execution. A Full Suite of Marketing Collateral: Comprehensive capability statement, look book and brochures designed to enhance FORGE's ability to succeed in every selling opportunity. An Incredible Video Launch: A high-impact brand reveal that engaged stakeholders, elevated FORGE's positioning, and set the stage for future growth. A Lead-Generation Website: A high-performance digital platform optimised for conversion, effectively driving engagement, inquiries, and business growth. The Results: A Future-Proofed Brand. With a renewed vision and strategic foundation, FORGE now stands as a national leader in outdoor infrastructure, ready to scale, innovate, and create lasting impact for Australian communities. Unlocking the outdoors. Building possibilities.

Community.name: NAV ECO
Community.description: NAV ECO. New Age Veneers. Navigating towards a Sustainable Future. ESG & CSR Strategic Framework. New Age Veneers (NAV) has always prioritised responsible sourcing and manufacturing, achieving certifications that attest to the ethical standards of its products. Building upon this foundation, NAV partnered with TOAST and together they launched NAV ECO, a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program rooted in eight United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UNSDGs). The program's mission is to guide NAV's team and operations towards more environmentally conscious decisions across all activities, ensuring that luxury and sustainability coexist harmoniously. Sectors: Community, Corporate, Environment, Sustainability. Services: Brand Architecture, Brand Positioning, Unique Value Proposition, Service Positioning, Brand Territory, Visual Identity, Brand Essence, Tone of Voice, Brand Guidelines, UX/UI, Web Design. Challenge: New Age Veneers needed to create a long-term sustainability strategic initiative that would not only align with global sustainability standards but also be deeply embedded in their core business practices. The challenge was to structure the program through an ESG framework and translate the CSR in a way that effectively communicates their commitment to ethical sourcing, environmental responsibility, and social impact while achieving measurable business KPIs. Furthermore, the CSR program needed to resonate with both internal teams and external stakeholders, from consumers to business partners. Solution: NAV ECO's objectives are driven by 8 UNSDGs, grouped into four key values: Harmony, Innovation, Equity, and Growth. Harmony: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being) and SDG 5 (Gender Equality) ensure balanced conditions for well-being and gender equity. Innovation: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) guide NAV's commitment to sustainable practices and innovative technologies. Equity: SDG 4 (Quality Education) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) provide equal opportunities for education and employment. Growth: SDG 15 (Life on Land) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) drive partnerships that promote environmental and economic sustainability. NAV ECO has become central to NAV's identity, showcasing its commitment to sustainability. The initiative reduces environmental impact through renewable energy, responsible production, and sustainable luxury products, enhancing NAV's brand reputation. It empowers teams to drive innovation and sustainability, resulting in stronger partnerships and increased lead generation. By aligning with UNSDGs, NAV is positioned as a leader in merging luxury with sustainability, contributing to economic growth and biodiversity conservation.

Community.name: Aryse
Community.description: Aryse. Brand Visualisation. Your Day, Your Way. ARYSE, a dynamic player in the disability support sector, engaged TOAST to transform their brand identity and digital presence to better serve NDIS participants, carers, and professionals in the industry. Our team collaborated with ARYSE to develop UI/UX/CX design and launch a new, user-centric website, alongside a dynamic brand identity applied to brochureware and environmental design, all aiming to make ARYSE a trusted name in a highly competitive market. Sectors: Health, Community. Services: Brand Positioning, Unique Value Proposition, Service Positioning, Brand Territory, Visual Identity, Brand Essence, Tone of Voice, Brand Guidelines, Stationery, Motion Graphics, UX/UI, Web Design. Solution: Grounded the insight that "a person living with a disability does not want to be defined by their abilities, but by who they are as a person," we crafted an empowering brand proposition around "Your Day, Your Way". This led to the creation of a brand identity that is as flexible, vibrant, and diverse as the community ARYSE serves. Our approach included developing user-centric design principles for their digital platforms and physical environments, enhancing the overall customer experience and engagement across all touchpoints.

Community.name: Greenhouse
Community.tagline: Connected. We Co-Innovate for Climate Action.
Community.description: Greenhouse — Investible. Brand Visualisation. Connected. We Co-Innovate for Climate Action. The effects of climate change are becoming rapidly evident. Higher temperatures, prolonged natural disasters and rising sea levels forecast for the coming decades. However, with these pressing issues come new opportunities for growth and innovation. The rapidly growing climate-focused technology sector, or 'climate-tech,' is seen as the solution to mitigating the lasting effects of our changing climate, with climate-tech innovation giving rise to entirely new industries that may well determine the future of our planet. Located in Sydney's brand new Salesforce Tower and created by Venture Capital group Investible, Greenhouse is an innovation ecosystem dedicated to accelerating the collaboration, adoption and impact of climate technologies on a global scale. Their core focus is addressing the issues and opportunities introduced by Climate Change through new climate-tech solutions. As part of a government initiative with the City of Sydney, Greenhouse provides affordable space for Australian scaleups to accelerate their expansion and connect with like-minded groups, investors and partners across the globe. Their vision being to unite multidisciplinary knowledge and accelerate the businesses that will help us respond to pressing climate challenges and capitalise on the opportunities therein. Challenge: Working with key stakeholders of the Investible team, TOAST was engaged to strategically design Greenhouse's innovative brand identity, creating a footprint that will generate awareness and boost global consideration for its climate-tech offerings. The Greenhouse brand needed to be respected by diverse key stakeholders and gain credibility among corporate companies - their number one key stakeholder for success. Through fostering a culture formed on disruption, Greenhouse endeavours to create & strengthen new ideas, connections and businesses. It is a place for growth and has a mission to provide climate-focused technology companies with the right expertise and connections to scale. TOAST's brand footprint and visual identity needed to harness this innovative power and unwavering ambition - and communicate it on a global scale. Solution: Strategic industry analysis, research and stakeholder workshops informed Greenhouse's overall brand footprint, building a brand that is optimised for growth and ingrained with modernity and creativity. Connecting groups, companies and visions in a multidisciplinary ecosystem, Greenhouse introduces the potential to create vast change through the immense power that is harnessed when working together. For Greenhouse, this comes to life through the power of 'co-innovation'. Reflecting this core brand value, TOAST crafted the tagline "Connected. We co-innovate for climate action," capturing their brand purpose of connecting the dots between people, ideas, and ultimately, countries, to co-create innovative solutions that will mitigate the effects of climate change. We mirrored their highly prolific, climate-focused world in a visual identity that draws inspiration from the cycle of the sun, the 'warming stripes' climate barcode and soft colour gradients within nature. Our design concept reflects the innate power within our natural, interconnected ecosystem and translates it into the collaborative community that Greenhouse fosters. Mirroring the agility and creativity within the business itself, the Greenhouse branding suite is versatile and highly dynamic. To reflect the 'revolutionary' approach of the brand, we utilised a free form colour gradient across the logotype and brand iconography. This gradient, with each colour connecting to 'co-create' something new, reflects Greenhouse's unstructured, creative approach to tackling climate issues. Complementing this, a halftone effect is applied across the brand, a graphic approach which reflects the 'connecting the dots' culture within Greenhouse and the myriad elements which make up its purpose, reach and impact. Beyond the visual territory, we sought to imbue their brand values across all aspects of the Greenhouse identity, exploring eco-fonts and climate-focused digital design. An eco-font minimises the consumption of ink and paper in print applications, and can reduce power usage by 30% in digital applications on Organic LED screens (increased further in combination with black backgrounds). Gilroy was selected as the Greenhouse typeface. Its sans-serif structure connotes modernity and innovation whilst its compact, clean line design equates to smaller file storage and fewer pixels when digitally presented. The introduction of an eco-font to Greenhouse's branding suite allows for a holistic representation of their brand values and emphasises the forward-thinking approach of their business. With understanding of the interrelationship between Masterbrand and a series of supporting programs and venues, a brand architecture was devised by TOAST and executed across all sub-brands. The signature colour gradient element of the Greenhouse masterbrand logo then became the common visual thread to unite a series of sub-brands, collaborating to execute the organisation's overall mission, with verticals including a climate tech hub, commercialisation booster 'Amped', the 'Greenhouse Challenge' program, and branding for climate supporters and venture capital investors.

Community.name: Sekisui House

Community.name: United Nations
Community.description: United Nations — United Nations Association of Australia. A Movement to Move the World Forward. United in Action. The United Nations turned 80 this year. To mark the milestone, they were looking to host a once-in-a-generation conference at Sydney's Sheraton Grand Hotel. NGOs, business leaders, academics and civil servants – the UN wanted to bring them all together for a day of talks, networking, collaboration, and defining the organisation's role in the 21st century. And it was a big deal. Many giants of Australian politics, like Penny Wong, Australian Minister for Foreign Affairs and Dr Anne Aly MP, Minister for Small Business, International Development and Multicultural Affairs, were booked to speak at the event. Challenge: So how were we going to get people to sign up? In recent years, there's a perception that the UN hasn't done enough to solve the modern world's biggest challenges: be that inequality, instability, insecurity or anything in-between. This meant we had to convince people that the conference was worth their while, and that it would be a forum for genuine action (not just talks). A chance to actually get things fixed, in one place, on one day, under one roof. Solution: To solve this problem, we asked ourselves: what does the UN do best? The answer: they unite people (the clue is in their name). For decades, they've brought people together as an international forum to solve major global challenges, from eradicating smallpox and reducing extreme poverty to defining the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Our work reminded people of this superpower, positioning the conference as a rare opportunity to join forces with other leading thinkers and make a tangible impact through collective action. #UnitedInAction became the rallying cry for the event, with messaging that flexed across speaker topics ("Unite for Human Rights", "Unite for Wildlife", "Unite for Facts' Sake") and showed people that they'd be helping to solve a range of issues by taking part. The sense of unity linked up our design system, too. The logo showed three circles interlocking into a single dynamic shape and the individual executions displayed policymakers, gamechangers and humanitarians standing shoulder to shoulder in solidarity. The campaign worked. It was a full house. The atmosphere was electric. And the event played a pivotal role in building alliances and shaping plans of action in multiple industries. A fitting way to mark 80 years of the United Nations.

Community.name: FORGE Website
Community.description: FORGE Website. Digital Transformation. Unlock the Outdoors. UNLOCKING A NEW ERA Demonstrating Deep Expertise Delivered at Scale. After five decades of excellence as Fleetwood, TOAST rebranded the company to FORGE, marking a new era for the brand. On the back of this dynamic evolution, TOAST transformed the business' website to perfectly position the team to expand its market share and continue delivering some of the largest and most exciting community infrastructure projects across the country. Through a comprehensive digital strategy that included competitive benchmarking, national industry research, involvement from key partners and senior-ranking Government stakeholders, TOAST thoroughly optimised FORGE's user experience. This deep dive into the company's methodologies and unique selling propositions informed a compelling new digital experience, aligning seamlessly with FORGE's strategic and commercial objectives. This evolution not only reflects the company's growth but also enhances its ability to meet and exceed the evolving needs of its partners, communities, and Government and corporate stakeholders. Challenge: In the realm of public infrastructure, the expectations from local governments, property developers, and communities are continually advancing. FORGE has led from the forefront of this movement, consistently delivering structures that not only deliver the necessary functional amenity, but leverages the opportunity for people to connect with the outdoors in ever more enriching and uplifting ways. But beyond the creative imagination of FORGE's awe-inspiring team lies deep knowledge and experience, a company that understands the importance of providing clients with certainty and confidence to execute major projects, addressing significant logistical, safety, and sustainability challenges at every phase. TOAST's task was to understand the needs and decision-levers of prospective clients securing vendors for major public outdoor amenity works, and position FORGE as the ideal partner to seamlessly and consistently deliver positive outcomes. This involved developing a UX/UI solution that achieved the delicate balance between the emotive appeal of FORGE's new brand proposition, "Unlock The Outdoors" crafted by TOAST, and the rational strengths of FORGE's comprehensive expertise and methodology, ensuring confidence and assurance in FORGE's capabilities. Solution: The FORGE website was meticulously crafted to reflect the company's leading role in delivering exceptional public infrastructure. The development process was rooted in a deep understanding of industry needs, derived from category insights and one-on-one interviews with corporate and government clients. This foundational research informed the UI/UX planning, ensuring that the website not only presents FORGE's major Unique Selling Propositions (USPs) but does so in a manner that instils confidence and underscores FORGE's capability for excellence in the sector. The website's user experience is a testament to the importance of thorough UX/UI planning and research. Each element of the interface has been designed with user engagement in mind, making information accessible and interactions intuitive. This strategic approach ensures that each visit to the website is informative, user-friendly, and reassuring, directly reflecting FORGE's expertise and reliability in transforming outdoor spaces. Through well-structured content and a thoughtfully designed user interface, the website effectively communicates FORGE's commitment to quality and their ability to meet the complex demands of modern public infrastructure projects.

Community.name: Grovia
Community.description: Grovia. Brand Visualisation. It's Time. Bioscientists, horticulturalists, and mechatronic engineers on a bold mission to accelerate ecosystem restoration at scale. Combining plant ecology expertise with world-class mechatronic engineering, AirSeed Technologies embarked on a transformative journey to evolve from a drone-based planting solution into grovia—an holistic land rehabilitation enabler unlocking ecosystem restoration at scale. Partnering with TOAST, grovia sought a brand identity that reflects its expanded mission while driving urgency and momentum around biodiversity restoration and climate action. Challenge: As a leading supplier of land rehabilitation strategy and implementation for governments and major corporations in the mining and resources sector, grovia required a robust and compelling brand identity. The goal was to establish a brand that encapsulated the company's scientific expertise, technological innovation, and commitment to ecological restoration while reinforcing the urgency of addressing biodiversity loss and climate change. This required a brand that would not only support grovia's evolution but also resonate with key stakeholders, driving engagement and trust in large-scale restoration efforts. Solution: To support grovia's business evolution, a strategic brand transformation was implemented. The new identity centres around a plant-inspired emblem, representing the four pillars of the business—science, people, technology, and nature. The tagline "It's Time" was introduced to instil a sense of urgency and momentum in tackling the climate crisis. The transformation began with brand immersion and competitor analysis to refine grovia's positioning within the industry. A comprehensive brand strategy was then developed to align with grovia's expanded capabilities and long-term vision. UI/UX/CX mapping was undertaken to enhance the digital user experience and customer engagement, resulting in a refreshed digital presence that effectively communicates grovia's mission and services. A revitalised brand identity was created to appeal to government agencies and corporations within the mining and resources sector. By integrating science, technology, and a deep commitment to environmental restoration, stands as a powerful force in land rehabilitation, equipped with a brand that reflects its mission and drives action at scale.

Community.name: Good Work Program
Community.description: Good Work Program. Governing Principles. CSR/ESG Framework. After working with Governing Principles to create the brand for their leading governance company, our teams partnered up again to enhance their brand new corporate brand with the development of a tailored CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) framework. This initiative aimed to elevate Governing Principles' business and align it with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while addressing economic, social, and environmental challenges. Challenge: Governing Principles recognised the critical importance of good governance in driving organisational success alongside the paramount integration of CSR principles into their operations to foster a sustainable and equitable world by 2030. They reached out to TOAST to create a CSR framework that not only upheld their values of integrity, transparency and ethical conduct but also created a positive social impact for their stakeholders. The challenge lay in developing a program that effectively addressed economic, social, and environmental challenges while aligning with the UN's SDGs to bring longevity and actionable vision to their brand. Solution: TOAST worked closely with Governing Principles to develop their framework, which together we titled the 'Good Work Program'. This tailored framework consists of three core pillars: Good Ethics, Good Wellbeing, and Good Employment. Each pillar is designed to address specific aspects of CSR and is strategically linked to corresponding United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. 1. Good Ethics: This pillar emphasises transparency, accountability, and ethical behaviour in all aspects of operations, aligning with Goal 16 - Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions. 2. Good Wellbeing: Focused on ensuring healthy lives and promoting wellbeing for all stakeholders, this pillar aligns with Goal 3 - Good Health and Wellbeing. 3. Good Employment: This pillar promotes inclusive and sustainable economic growth, aligning with Goal 8 - Decent Work and Economic Growth. The design of the Good Work Program is an iconography set that draws directly from the graphic language of Governing Principles' corporate brand image. This approach enables optimum brand equity and positions their CSR framework as a core vertical of their business operations. The 'Good Work Program' not only enhances Governing Principles' brand reputation but also builds trust with stakeholders by actively contributing to sustainable development initiatives outlined by the United Nations. It demonstrates Governing Principles' commitment to excellence in corporate social responsibility while making a meaningful difference in their work environments and communities - showcasing how aligning with CSR principles can lead to enduring success in a thriving corporate ecosystem.

Community.name: United We Shine
Community.description: United We Shine. WWF Australia. Campaign Development. As the world shifts to a low carbon future, Australia has everything we need to take the lead and become a renewable energy export superpower. We've got endless sunshine, plenty of space, powerful winds, world-class expertise and strong trade relationships: it's a winning combination. The twin crises of the 2019/2020 bushfires and the Covid-19 pandemic have created a need for a recovery package that helps the country rebuild. WWF-Australia is calling on our leaders to make Australia the world's leading exporter of renewable energy by 2030. [Page contains no additional prose; the Challenge and Solution sections are present as labels only with no body text.]

Community.name: Innovation for Impact
Community.description: CSR/ESG Framework. Elevating the award winning strategic brand platform that TOAST completed for the Inovi team in 2023, our teams collaborated once again to embark on defining a tailored CSR framework that emulates the future-focused vision of the Inovi brand and the team behind it. Inovi is a prominent player in the commercial construction sector and introducing a CSR program to their business is leading them on a transformative journey towards sustainability and social responsibility. Strategised by TOAST through extensive workshopping sessions, their program "Innovation for Impact" is rooted in the pillars of 'In,' 'Ov,' and 'I,' and represents Inovi's commitment to integrating sustainability practices, prioritising employee wellbeing, and making a positive impact on communities and cities. Challenge: Introducing a CSR program to their business provides a framework for both their short and long term goals on both an internal and external level. The company recognised that merely transitioning to environmentally friendly procedures and materials wasn't enough; thus a comprehensive CSR strategy was what was needed to drive meaningful change across its business lines. Incorporating it into an already bustling business, TOAST faced the challenge of aligning Inovi's operations with sustainable practices while ensuring the wellbeing of its employees and positively impacting the communities it serves, all under the one program. Solution: Drawing on the similar rationale behind their brand name, the Inovi CSR program was titled "Innovation for Impact" and has three key verticals: 'In,' (Innovation at the Core) 'Ov,' (Overall Wellbeing of Our People) and 'I,' (Impact on Cities and Community). These respectively represent Inovi's commitment to integrating sustainability practices, prioritising employee wellbeing and making a positive impact on communities and cities. Ensuring we created a lasting, robust platform that gave the Inovi team vision and guidance in their CSR / ESG endeavours, each pillar is associated with 3 key United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, providing the Inovi team with a clear and actionable path. The double circle symbol of the Innovation for Impact program represents the Inovi brand through a trademarked icon. Carried through for the CSR program 'Innovation for Impact', this design injects Inovi's absolute dedication to creating a lasting, positive impact within their team and wider community as a key undercurrent of their brand identity. The primary CSR logo for Inovi employs a greyscale palette (warm & dark grey), culminating in a clean and distinct brand identity that effectively embodies the focus and commitment within the brand. When developed into the 3 pillars, brighter more recognisable tones are introduced. The colour palette for CSR remains consistent with the master brand, yet with modifications in colour hierarchy. Greys take on a more pronounced role, accompanied by the addition of the three colours specific to each category. This strategic approach enhances brand recognition and positions CSR as a distinct division of the business. Through the tailored CSR program, "Innovation for Impact," Inovi has successfully addressed the challenge of integrating sustainability, prioritising employee wellbeing, and making a positive impact on communities, but not as a one-off claim, as a framework with vision, longevity and lasting relevance. By embracing innovation, fostering a supportive work environment, and actively engaging with communities, Inovi sets a benchmark for responsible and sustainable business practices in the commercial construction industry.

Community.name: Centre for Pain Impact
Community.description: Understanding pain to cure it. Centre for Pain IMPACT is a pioneering initiative driven by a team of psychologists and neuroscientists dedicated to revolutionising the field of chronic pain research. With a mission to disrupt traditional approaches and advance towards finding a cure, the organisation stands at the forefront of innovation and collaboration. Rooted in the belief that comprehensive understanding leads to effective solutions, Centre for Pain IMPACT is committed to empowering individuals to reclaim their lives from the grips of chronic pain. As a brand integrated in the NeuRA research group, IMPACT needed to build their own identity and create a recognisable brand for themselves. Challenge: Despite significant advancements in medical science, chronic pain remains a pervasive and debilitating condition for millions worldwide. The challenge lies in not only managing the symptoms but also in unravelling the complex underlying mechanisms of pain. Traditional approaches often fall short in providing holistic solutions tailored to individual experiences. Centre for Pain IMPACT recognised the need for a paradigm shift in how chronic pain is understood, managed and ultimately cured. The challenge that TOAST was engaged to solve was to establish a brand identity that reflects their innovative spirit, collaborative ethos and unwavering commitment to making a meaningful impact on people's lives. Solution: At the heart of Centre for Pain IMPACT's brand identity is the essence of understanding and validating pain as the key to unlocking effective solutions. This mantra not only reflects their scientific approach but also underscores their empathy and dedication to validating the experiences of those affected by chronic pain. Their team engages with scientists, academics, clinicians and individuals impacted by chronic pain to foster an environment of collective intelligence and shared purpose. In this way, they embrace innovation and disruption, challenging the status quo in pain research. Their brand thus communicates a bold and forward-thinking approach, signalling their readiness to explore new avenues and push boundaries in pursuit of a cure. Above all, their brand narrative is about empowering individuals to reclaim their lives from the shackles of chronic pain. By providing tailored solutions and fostering a sense of agency, they aim to make a tangible impact on the lives of those they serve. These core values of IMPACT culminated in a brand identity that is entirely people-focused. With a colour palette of softened vibrant tones interwoven with individual and group-based imagery assets, the identity symbolises IMPACT's comprehensive healthcare approach and their focus on the complete wellbeing of individuals with chronic pain. The logotype incorporates a stylised image of two hands coming together, a symmetric design which reinforces the idea of a coordinated and integrated approach to healthcare and reflects the collaboration between medical experts and patients, working together towards a common goal of pain relief and improved quality of life. Through a strategic brand design process, Centre for Pain IMPACT has successfully established a cohesive brand identity that resonates with their stakeholders and embodies their mission to disrupt, innovate, and ultimately cure chronic pain.

Community.name: CAW.SYD
Community.description: Change Through Action. Climate Action Week Sydney 2024 (CAW SYD) was held from 13-19 May and is an annual, global event pulsating with activities in the heart of the City of Sydney. The week encompasses a series of community-led events from all aspects of the climate action ecosystem to bring together like minded individuals, groups and changemakers to amplify the discourse around climate action. As part of the dedicated brand/marketing planning committee including The Being Group, Edge Impact, Greenhouse and Investible, TOAST collaborated on the visionary development and delivery of 2024's Climate Action Week Sydney. Our team was instrumental in crafting the brand framework and identity for the event, a design so impactful that it has also been used for CAW SYD 2025. We are thrilled to see our vision continue to shape and inspire this vital movement. Challenge: The challenge for TOAST was to create a strategic framework and visual identity that captures the essence of Climate Action Week Sydney and resonates with diverse audiences. The goal was to foster an inclusive Australian Grassroots Movement engaging with all walks of life, promote connection, collaboration and commitment to supporting climate action and establish a distinctive CAW SYD identity solidifying Sydney's global leadership in sustainability. Solution: TOAST crafted a dynamic visual identity for CAW SYD that underscores the transformative beauty of change through action and the power of togetherness for a common goal. With a vibrant and adaptable colour scheme, this concept revolves around the collective power of societal action and displays the resounding transformations that can incur from even the simplest of movements. The design is elevated by dynamic graphic elements, infused with colour and emotion to underscore the wealth of opportunity inherent in Sydney's innovative cityscape and reveal the ideas, passion and vision abundant in the community. The strategic framework aimed to establish a platform for ongoing engagement and collaboration, emphasising traditional knowledge, engaging neighbouring nations and ensuring diverse, accessible initiatives, reflecting Sydney's global outlook. This framework underlines CAW SYD as a dynamic climate action event, uniting professionals and communities to engage in discussions and innovatively tackle global climate issues. With the strategic framework and visual identity created by TOAST, Climate Action Week Sydney has amplified the City of Sydney's role in addressing the urgent need for climate action. It embarks on a transformative journey toward becoming a green and inclusive city while fostering a Climate Action Ecosystem that engages all stakeholders and reflects Sydney's commitment to a sustainable future. TOAST is overjoyed to be a founding member of Climate Action Week Sydney and to be part of a growing network of Future Makers across the world.

Community.name: Earth Hour x EPSON
Community.description: A Simple Switch. Epson, world-leading printing and electronics manufacturer, is a trailblazer in the corporate world for their rigorous sustainability goals and measures. Their commitment to the environment began close to 80 years ago and is stronger than ever today. Their product designs and business decisions focus on low energy consumption, minimised waste, small environmental footprints, high reliability and minimal moving parts. Epson's environmentally focused vision coincides with the mission of WWF's annual campaign Earth Hour and that of our global branding team here at TOAST - all seeking to create a better, greener future for our planet. Bringing together these like minded teams, WWF Singapore and our TOAST team worked with Epson to spearhead a sub-campaign for Earth Hour 2024. As Earth Hour's first international corporate partner, the collaboration between Epson, TOAST and WWF has created an invaluable partnership as we embark on a mission to amplify Earth Hour's message and encourage collective action towards sustainability. Challenge: The primary challenge of this sub-campaign lay in rallying global, cross-demographic support and engagement to foster a unified movement towards a sustainable planet. Working across 3 time zones and uniting 20+ passionate individuals, TOAST, Epson and WWF-Singapore faced the task of inspiring individuals and communities worldwide to actively participate in Earth Hour's mission. Additionally, the emphasis on community involvement required strategies that resonated at both local and global levels. Collaboration across diverse stakeholders and aligning with Epson's existing initiatives, added depth and complexity to the project, necessitating seamless alignment of objectives and approaches. Solution: The sub-campaign for Epson was aptly named 'A Simple Switch', symbolising the small yet impactful changes all individuals can make to support environmental conservation efforts. By simply making a slight switch in our daily habits, we can have a great combined impact on our environment. TOAST's involvement in the campaign was enormously comprehensive, beginning with a 2-day strategic alignment session for the three teams in Singapore. Emile, our Head of Strategy, ran two 6 hour collaborative sessions with the Epson team. This involved strategic visioning and campaign development - pivotal moves for aligning all stakeholders towards a unified vision and approach. Using the defined campaign concept of 'A Simple Switch', The Toasties leveraged our expertise in script writing, storyboarding and video production to create compelling video campaigns that captured the essence of Earth Hour's message and highlighted Epson's dedication to sustainability through its #MakeTheSwitch campaign. A comprehensive social media strategy devised by TOAST and WWF ensured maximum outreach, amplifying Earth Hour's impact and raising awareness of Epson's sustainability initiatives on a global scale. Recognising the importance of internal alignment within Epson's team for the roll out and comprehension of the campaign, with WWF, TOAST produced valuable documentation and resources, including a campaign communications guideline, operations manual and detailed employee e-handbook. These resources empowered Epson's team to champion the campaign internally and externally, ensuring alignment with the campaign's objectives and Earth Hour's initiatives. Beyond the immediate campaign objectives, the collaboration fostered a lasting legacy of partnership and innovation in the fight against climate change. By harnessing the collective power of creativity, technology and environmental advocacy, the collaboration exemplified the transformative potential of cross-sector partnerships in addressing global challenges. In an era defined by environmental urgency, the collaboration between TOAST, Epson and WWF-Singapore stands as a beacon of hope and progress. Through strategic alignment, creative execution and a shared unwavering environmental commitment, our three teams demonstrated the power of collaboration in driving meaningful change. And as the world continues to grapple with environmental challenges, this campaign partnership serves as a testament to the transformative impact that can be achieved when organisations unite towards a common purpose: to create a more sustainable future for generations to come. The collaboration between WWF-Singapore, TOAST, and Epson resulted in a resounding success, with the 'A Simple Switch' sub-campaign making a significant impact on raising awareness and driving action for sustainability. WWF-Singapore is open to develop more meaningful partnerships for now and the future.

Community.name: Earth Hour
Community.tagline: Switch off. Give an hour for Earth.
Community.description: Switch off. Give an hour for Earth. Earth Hour, the largest environmental grassroots movement in the world, is a household name for environmentally conscious activities. First taking place via its famed 'switch off' campaign in 2007, Earth Hour has grown to be an annual celebration and epicentre for coming together for our environment and doing activities we enjoy which protect and preserve our Earth. In a powerful collaboration, TOAST is utterly overjoyed to be working with WWF International's Singapore team as part of the team behind Earth Hour 2024. This alliance signifies a shared commitment to environmental sustainability, community engagement, and a vision for a more eco-conscious future. The collaboration draws on TOAST's strategic branding expertise and Earth Hour's global influence, our collaboration has helped amplify the campaign's impact, so much so that our design and branding will continue to be used for Earth Hour 2025. Challenge: The challenge for the 2024 campaign lies in maximising recognition and engagement to foster a global movement towards a sustainable planet. TOAST and Earth Hour faced the task of inspiring individuals and communities worldwide to actively participate in Earth Hour's mission to protect the planet. Additionally, the emphasis on community involvement requires strategies that resonate at both local and global levels. This campaign involved multi-level global collaboration across a number of months. Ideation sessions, seminars and interviews needed to take place for this to come to life effectively and efficiently. Solution: TOAST's innovative strategies, including cutting-edge digital campaigns and compelling storytelling, are at the forefront of the solution. As Future Makers, our team at TOAST is committed to adopting new methodologies, questioning our internal viewpoints and challenging the status quo in order to make a statement and encourage change. The collaboration between WWF Singapore's Earth Hour team and TOAST here in Sydney leverages our creative ingenuity to develop narratives and visuals that captivate diverse audiences, ensuring global resonance. The key solution this year lay in mobilising communities from grassroots initiatives to global events, encouraging participation in ways that align with the overarching goal of sustainability and showcasing that everyday activities, that we already participate in and enjoy, are in fact actions that help our planet. Collaborating over 6 months, TOAST worked with the Earth Hour team in Singapore to visualise this year's concept through captivating video content (featuring none other than Ed Sheeran!). Following the Earth Hour style guide, we worked closely to develop multiple scripts that communicated the 2024 mission, ensuring they were punchy, accessible and globally relevant. This was converted into both Radio and Video content where we created detailed storyboards and developed custom graphic elements and transitions to build a story around the 2024 concept, encouraging the globe to #GiveAnHourForEarth. The TOAST and Earth Hour collaboration for the 2024 campaign is a fusion of creativity, passion and purpose. Together, we are striving to create ripples of positive change, leaving an indelible mark on the global community. The solution lies in transformative strategies that redefine the narrative of environmental initiatives, inspiring a collective commitment to a sustainable future!

Community.name: The Know
Community.tagline: Australian Emerging Drug Information & Resources Hub
Community.description:
The Know — NCCRED PRN. Brand Visualisation. Australian Emerging Drug Information & Resources Hub. Recreational drug use is common practice worldwide. With various ‘illicit’ drugs becoming easier to access and, in some cases, decriminalised, their usage is continuing to rise. With this comes rising cases of drug overdose, potential poisoning and long term harm to users’ health. Incidents of such harm resulting from recreational use or heavy usage can be mitigated, and even avoided entirely, if information is readily available on drugs’ safety. This is the founding mission of NCCRED’s Prompt Response Network and their newly crafted online platform ‘The Know’. Designed to provide free, up-to-date and judgement-free advice or alerts about the harm factor or legitimacy of current drug strains in the community, The Know will inform users of toxic chemicals and cases of lacing or the illegitimacy of emerging illicit drugs. Through their Prompt Response Network (PRN), NCCRED runs several programs related to emerging drugs. Their programs deliver harm reduction services, helping to develop nuanced understandings around emerging drugs (and drugs in general) used among our communities, and empowering the people affected, and the general public, with relevant information through alerts.

Challenge: Worldwide, incidents of drug abuse and drug-related accidents are increasing as people experiment with emerging drugs and the strengths increase of ‘old-school’ drugs. Such harms can be prevented and reduced by the timely sharing of accurate, relevant information. TOAST was approached by NCCRED’s PRN platform to assess this situation, looking at how information can be made accessible and clearly understood whilst remaining accurate for all Australian communities. In this vein, our team was engaged to strategise, design and launch a public-facing brand which will act as a trusted and highly reliable source of information to help reduce harm across the drug landscape in Australia. From the outset of this project, we recognised that reduction of drug use was not PRN’s core goal. Their goal was to provide accurate and up-to-date information to reduce the negative consequences that arise from drug misinformation and the consumption of compromised strains. The brand’s core purpose was to shift the narrative on drugs; supportive and open-minded values needed to be at the heart of the messaging. TOAST needed to create an altruistic brand which can be trusted. Our challenge was around building an influential platform which would be successful in engaging diverse audience groups on such a critical matter.

Solution: PRN exists to improve the health and wellbeing of Australians who partake in recreational or heavy drug use, aiming to prevent and minimise drug-related harm. Developed by a network of mixed contributors, including people who use drugs, bystanders, government bodies, and medical organisations, their new service provides access to a unique, accurate and timely source of information on emerging drugs and safe drug use. To create a brand platform that is relevant, recognisable and ownable by PRN, TOAST delved deep into their space, interviewing a vast array of community groups, from recreational drug users, sober ex-users and festival attendees, to policy makers, GPs and coroners. It was paramount that our branding resonated across multiple targets, peak bodies and locations. Having myriad audiences, our team needed to formulate a broad yet targeted brand approach, one that is flexible and provides user-centric information. PRN’s overall focus on harm reduction respects that you can use drugs and reduce potential harm, without abstinence. They are there to support and assist, not punish. A ‘people first attitude’ is core to their DNA and needed to be central to their new service’s brand footprint. Building on this, we crafted their brand and communications suite to be judgement-free - focusing solely on awareness, education, and respect. TOAST crafted a brand platform that is for people who actively use drugs, for the general public, and for professionals. Allowing drug safety information to be accessible by users, relatives and the general public, whilst also delivering a platform for the police, coroners and GPs which consolidates information to aid in policy making, trials or clinical studies. The visual identity was strongly based on insights from our qualitative user testing and interview process, wherein preferences arose for a design that did not induce shame or embarrassment and used clean layouts to allow for information to be easily understood. Logotype preferences were for a word that was simple and memorable, connoting “information sharing” or “harm reduction,” paired with a realistic, trustworthy image. Common Cause Australia’s ‘Drug Stigma Message Guide’ declared that “messages based around altruistic and community-oriented values including honesty, helpfulness and equality, were significantly more effective at activating supportive attitudes in persuadable audiences than purely fact-based messages.” Insights which led to our big idea ‘Keeping you in the know,’ which was subsequently moulded for the platform’s name ‘The Know.’ ‘Keeping (users) in the know’ is about keeping them informed and mindful, providing knowledge on dangerous drug strains and more broadly on the side effects of recreational or recurrent drug usage. Users are kept in the know through having access to accurate, comprehensive and timely information which can save lives. Beyond their pill imagery, the connected circles within The Know’s logotype are founded on a conceptual framework underpinned by community connection, collaboration and support, and the colour-blocked design highlighting ‘now’ in a contrasting orange reflects the urgency, accuracy and immediacy of their services. The primary colour palette of Purple, Orange and Green is deliberately dissimilar to the typical blue of medical and law enforcement industries to create a safe space that is not connected with punishment or pain - building on the ‘judgement-free’ aspect of their brand narrative - with purple, orange and green chosen specifically for their symbolism of wisdom, change and growth, respectively. TOAST developed this brand identity across The Know’s corporate presence, creating a cohesive brand suite and initial social media Look & Feel. Working in such a sensitive, and dangerous, environment, we focused deeply on the human-to-human dynamic of our brand design. Paying close attention to our use of language and imagery to not induce shame or create further stigma through our discourse. The Know connects individuals with the information to make safer choices, providing inspiration, knowledge and an action plan for improving individual and societal health outcomes, and saving lives.

Community.name: Anavo
Community.description:
Anavo — The Polyglot Group. Brand Visualisation. The energy to do better. Anavo, a subsidiary of The Polyglot Group, is a global Recruitment Agency specialising in industries focused on Renewable Energy, Environmental action, and Sustainability. Operating in 6 countries, spanning 9 time zones and 4 continents, they partner with clients, from large multinational corporations through to local SMEs, providing access to leading talents across the globe to bring climate action industry projects to life. Their mission is to help with Permanent Recruitment, Project & Specialist Hire, Global Mobility, Executive Search & Temporary recruitment for climate-focused sectors. They partner with some of the most innovative, high-growth companies in the environmental / sustainability sector, to match them with exceptional talent. Anavo creates a bridge between businesses & talent to empower individuals and teams to drive the decarbonising change that our planet urgently requires.

Challenge: TOAST was called upon by The Polyglot Group to create an engaging, progressive, and friendly brand footprint that encapsulates their new company’s vision. The challenge for TOAST to reach, through strategic brand messaging, was “how are we going to engage companies in the sustainability market as well as individual job seekers passionate about and searching for employment in the environmental industry?” It was crucial for Anavo’s final brand to be accessible and recognisable. Not only to stand out as a key player in the recruitment realm, but primarily as champions for sustainability. They need to be known by companies working across the environment/future/net-zero space as well as respected by individuals who are passionate about working collectively toward progressive green action, and by global corporate bodies aiming to expand their business values to reflect a sustainable future.

Solution: The company needed to be recognised as a group that is driven by passion and a dedication to a wider cause. Through an iterative research process of interviews, industry analysis and an in-depth strategic workshop, our team developed Anavo’s unique brand footprint which aligned the visions of all key stakeholders and brought their business values to life. Inspired by the Greek word which means “to ignite,” “Anávo” was chosen for the brand name, encompassing their mission as a collective to instigate positive change and help the world transition to cleaner practices for a better future. Accompanying this, TOAST put forth the tagline “The Energy to do better” for their team to adopt. This showcases to their audience that they are a recruitment agency empowering people within the clean energy & environment industries to drive the decarbonising change that our planet needs. The logo that was settled on encompasses the bright ambition intrinsic to renewable energy. The buoyant typeface design reflects that they are a team who is passionate about going the extra mile and encapsulates their deep expertise that is underpinned by a curiosity for new ideas, systems and innovations. At only 2 years old, having been created amidst the uncertain yet innovation-provoking time of the 2020 pandemic, Anavo already has a 10+ local employment team, a 15,000+ LinkedIn network and an extensive library of successful client case studies. Their team has supported the growth ambitions and sustainability goals of global companies such as: Enphase Energy, Akuo Energy, Cress Consulting, SMA Solar Technology, Yingli Green Energy. This rapid growth not only reflects the success of TOAST’s branding suite, our team being responsible for Anavo’s brand narrative, strategic footprint and visual identity, but the deep necessity for a platform such as this.

Community.name: Community
Community.description: Community. Sekisui House. Sanctuary Masterplan. A place for all. The Sekisui House philosophy 'Love of Humanity', integrated with the ancient Japanese cultural principle of Satoyama 'Harmony between the environment and nature,' has guided Sanctuary's design to reflect the benefits of co-dependence between people, nature, and the built environment. Sanctuary places a deep respect for community at the heart of its design and development. It's about weaving nature throughout, the connectivity to the residents, and linkages to the broader community and Sydney as a whole. With a key focus on 'Michi' or 'Spatial Design Experience' Sanctuary's brand has emerged with the need to evolve and appeal to become a centre of life for people. The incorporation of design, innovation and technology with the natural surroundings through the facilities, landscapes and amenities, plays an essential role in the uniqueness of Sanctuary. Vibrant, fulfilling interactions between people, place and nature bring to life a beautiful spirit of community that occurs within and beyond its boundaries. Challenge: The vision for Sanctuary was to create a masterplanned community where a genuine respect for nature is reignited, and where a harmonious relationship between people and built form is nurtured; Sanctuary is a space that is designed to facilitate community connection. Sekisui House's core design principles and community-building ethos uplift the offering of this masterplan and introduce endless benefits that will elevate the lives of all in Wentworth Point. Maximising parkland within the site, expanding retail opportunities, integrating public transport and offering a calendar of community events at the foreshore park; what was once merely the end of the road is now becoming the heart of a revitalised community. Along with creating opportunities for community activity, the connection to the landscape offers boundless benefits to mental and physical health. By delivering a unique residential and community precinct that is at one with nature, Sanctuary will help its residents experience enriched, fulfilling lives that evolve with time and last for generations. Solution: To encapsulate the deep community spirit that Sekisui House has created through Sanctuary, TOAST crafted the tagline 'A place for all,' championing the neighbourly connections and inclusive atmosphere that Sanctuary fosters. This masterplan generates coexistence and co-prosperity by increasing the amount of public open space, and interactive activity areas for the whole community of Wentworth Point to enjoy. Offering more than 6 football-field's worth of public parkland and open space, over 4km of cycling and pedestrian-friendly paths, and with 34% of the entire masterplan dedicated to public green space, Sanctuary is undeniably alive with experiences and possibilities. This is a precinct designed to facilitate community connection, neighbourly interaction, and easy engagement with your native environment. Reflecting the core brand values of 'vibrant interactions' and 'comfortable living,' this approach delivers a unique experience for residents and the greater community, creating cohesion and instilling life, energy & vibrancy.

Community.name: Juror
Community.description: Juror. NSW Department of Justice. Observe Listen Decide. The NSW Government's Department of Justice orchestrates the state's compulsory jury service. Juries are used to ensure that legal verdicts are impartial and in line with community standards of behaviour. Serving as a juror is a mandatory role, providing unique insights into the NSW court process. Juries are used in the NSW District Court and NSW Supreme Court to determine criminal and civil matters. People aged over 18 are summoned and subsequently randomly selected to serve on a jury in a particular trial. The process of collating, storing and selecting names of all eligible jurors is a large task which occurs year-round. TOAST was engaged to assist with the ideation and design of an updated user interface and communications platform which simplifies the process on both the distribution and client end. Challenge: The juror selection process is a key part of the Australian justice system. Every year, the names of approximately 200,000 potential jurors are randomly selected from the NSW Electoral Roll and included on the jury list. From this number, up to 150,000 people will be summoned to present to court, with a subsequent 9,000 being selected to fulfil their service on a jury panel. TOAST was tasked with renewing a user management system to reduce the bulk of content and business hours required to orchestrate the juror selection process. Given the evidenced high amount of data being dealt with in the NSW Department of Justice, TOAST worked to strengthen the brand and streamline their processes, aiming to reduce pain points and simplify processes for both the distribution teams and summoned jurors. Solution: TOAST designed a two-part solution with an updated User Interface Design and a Communications Suite. Our team created the overall design for the Department of Justice's online portal, mobile application and management system for jurors and potential jurors, known as Juror. This Jury Management System is an updated user database storing information on NSW jurors and contains algorithms that are used to randomly select the 200,000 jurors each year from the four million-strong NSW electoral roll. With its algorithm for random selection, the system dramatically simplifies the Jury summoning process and provides efficiencies throughout the entire procedure for Jurors and Government alike. In line with this, TOAST crafted a marketing communications suite for the NSW public. Our strategy led us to develop a concept that portrayed a sense of pride and civic duty gained from participation in NSW's Jury Service. Our Big Idea came down to the three verbs "Observe, Listen, Decide." This slogan works hand-in-hand with the authentic imagery, showcasing real people across NSW to portray a sense of ownership, responsibility and recognition for the cause. At the 2017 Sydney Design Awards, TOAST received a Gold Award in the Government Service category for our Juror campaign on behalf of the Department of Justice.

Community.name: Laguna & Glade
Community.description: Laguna & Glade. Sekisui House. Sanctuary - Stage Two. Life Ever Changing. The Sanctuary masterplan in Wentworth Point offers an ever-changing life experience through people, culture and the environments within. Following the completion and success of ‘Landing,’ Stage 1 of Sanctuary, the masterplan is moving forward to its second stage. Positioned to be overlooking the Parramatta River and bordering the neighbourhood green, Stage 2 lies at the very centre of Sanctuary's vibrant community estate and encompasses three new elements, the Laguna and Glade residences and Revive health club. Consisting of 171 premium waterside apartments centred around lush open spaces and a multilevel wellbeing facilities building - Revive, the Laguna and Glade residences achieve perfect synergy with nature. This stage is beautifully designed to allow an inside-out communication between landscape and architecture. Embracing the calm, curious flow of the Parramatta River and the best of international living standards, these developments have been designed to allow seamless communication between the surrounding natural landscape and modern architecture. Challenge: As Laguna, Glade and Revive are staged additions in a large-scale masterplan, as opposed to standalone developments, it was imperative that the Sanctuary property branding and strategic vision remained as the common thread that ties all elements together. As, to remain an authentic and highly-regarded brand, it is key to present a united image with a consistent and clear message. Harmony, vibrancy, a sense of calm and liveability are fundamental attributes defining a sanctuary and are wonderfully evident in this Stage 2 development. The Laguna and Glade residences and Revive health club bring newfound energy and life to the Sanctuary precinct. Aligned and connected with the overall branding and message of Sanctuary’s masterplan, Laguna and Glade have an infectious spirit. In the heart of the precinct, bookended by both the river and neighbourhood green, these spaces weave beautifully into their natural surrounds and offer occupants a space that is liveable and abundant in lively characteristics. As elements within the Sanctuary masterplan brand, Laguna, Glade and Revive are similarly identifiable by the unique kaleidoscopic logotype. In creating this gracefully fragmented circular imagery, TOAST was inspired by the fundamental principles within Japanese design, such as simplicity, understated beauty and tranquillity. It’s an intricate but elegant wreath, a symbol which ties all elements of Sanctuary together. Solution: Laguna and Glade are highly anticipated boutique developments on the water’s edge offering a serene living experience in the heart of Sanctuary. Across both buildings, nature acts as a bridge between the apartments and the wider landscape, creating an unrivalled living experience where nature and urban living seamlessly integrate. The harmony and communication between our inside and outside worlds is a fundamental element within Sanctuary’s brand footprint, making this masterplan evermore unique. The fluidity of Laguna’s logo variant captures the sense of calm and serenity that the building exudes. The malleable, rejuvenating qualities of water are captured in the building's architecture and are further conveyed in this logo's expression. As for Glade, this logo variant is heavily flora-inspired and integrates natural influences throughout its design. The striking green textural pattern conveys this sense of vitality, promising a life that is energetic and connected to nature. Further, Revive's logo takes the aqueous territory introduced with Laguna and pushes it further. Centred around the uniquely styled, revitalising pool that is a core foundation of the building's offerings, this logo treatment fully reflects the tranquil, restorative qualities of the health club it represents. The Stage 2 triad is an extension of the refuge that is Sanctuary and delivers a beautifully unique experience for residents and the wider community.
