By simply making a slight switch in our daily habits, we can have a great combined impact on our environment. TOAST's involvement in the campaign was enormously comprehensive, beginning with a 2-day strategic alignment session for the three teams in Singapore. Emile, our Head of Strategy, ran two 6 hour collaborative sessions with the Epson team. This involved strategic visioning and campaign development - pivotal moves for aligning all stakeholders towards a unified vision and approach. Using the defined campaign concept of 'A Simple Switch', The Toasties leveraged our expertise in script writing, storyboarding and video production to create compelling video campaigns that captured the essence of Earth Hour's message and highlighted Epson's dedication to sustainability through its #MakeTheSwitch campaign. A comprehensive social media strategy devised by TOAST and WWF ensured maximum outreach, amplifying Earth Hour's impact and raising awareness of Epson's sustainability initiatives on a global scale. Recognising the importance of internal alignment within Epson's team for the roll out and comprehension of the campaign, with WWF, TOAST produced valuable documentation and resources, including a campaign communications guideline, operations manual and detailed employee e-handbook. These resources empowered Epson's team to champion the campaign internally and externally, ensuring alignment with the campaign's objectives and Earth Hour's initiatives. Beyond the immediate campaign objectives, the collaboration fostered a lasting legacy of partnership and innovation in the fight against climate change. By harnessing the collective power of creativity, technology and environmental advocacy, the collaboration exemplified the transformative potential of cross-sector partnerships in addressing global challenges. In an era defined by environmental urgency, the collaboration between TOAST, Epson and WWF-Singapore stands as a beacon of hope and progress. Through strategic alignment, creative execution and a shared unwavering environmental commitment, our three teams demonstrated the power of collaboration in driving meaningful change. And as the world continues to grapple with environmental challenges, this campaign partnership serves as a testament to the transformative impact that can be achieved when organisations unite towards a common purpose: to create a more sustainable future for generations to come. The collaboration between WWF-Singapore, TOAST, and Epson resulted in a resounding success, with the 'A Simple Switch' sub-campaign making a significant impact on raising awareness and driving action for sustainability. WWF-Singapore is open to develop more meaningful partnerships for now and the future.

Non-Profit.name: Earth Hour
Non-Profit.tagline: Switch off. Give an hour for Earth.
Non-Profit.description: Switch off. Give an hour for Earth. Earth Hour, the largest environmental grassroots movement in the world, is a household name for environmentally conscious activities. First taking place via its famed 'switch off' campaign in 2007, Earth Hour has grown to be an annual celebration and epicentre for coming together for our environment and doing activities we enjoy which protect and preserve our Earth. In a powerful collaboration, TOAST is utterly overjoyed to be working with WWF International's Singapore team as part of the team behind Earth Hour 2024. This alliance signifies a shared commitment to environmental sustainability, community engagement, and a vision for a more eco-conscious future. The collaboration draws on TOAST's strategic branding expertise and Earth Hour's global influence, our collaboration has helped amplify the campaign's impact, so much so that our design and branding will continue to be used for Earth Hour 2025. Challenge: The challenge for the 2024 campaign lies in maximising recognition and engagement to foster a global movement towards a sustainable planet. TOAST and Earth Hour faced the task of inspiring individuals and communities worldwide to actively participate in Earth Hour's mission to protect the planet. Additionally, the emphasis on community involvement requires strategies that resonate at both local and global levels. This campaign involved multi-level global collaboration across a number of months. Ideation sessions, seminars and interviews needed to take place for this to come to life effectively and efficiently. Solution: TOAST's innovative strategies, including cutting-edge digital campaigns and compelling storytelling, are at the forefront of the solution. As Future Makers, our team at TOAST is committed to adopting new methodologies, questioning our internal viewpoints and challenging the status quo in order to make a statement and encourage change. The collaboration between WWF Singapore's Earth Hour team and TOAST here in Sydney leverages our creative ingenuity to develop narratives and visuals that captivate diverse audiences, ensuring global resonance. The key solution this year lay in mobilising communities from grassroots initiatives to global events, encouraging participation in ways that align with the overarching goal of sustainability and showcasing that everyday activities, that we already participate in and enjoy, are in fact actions that help our planet. Collaborating over 6 months, TOAST worked with the Earth Hour team in Singapore to visualise this year's concept through captivating video content (featuring none other than Ed Sheeran!). Following the Earth Hour style guide, we worked closely to develop multiple scripts that communicated the 2024 mission, ensuring they were punchy, accessible and globally relevant. This was converted into both Radio and Video content where we created detailed storyboards and developed custom graphic elements and transitions to build a story around the 2024 concept, encouraging the globe to #GiveAnHourForEarth. The TOAST and Earth Hour collaboration for the 2024 campaign is a fusion of creativity, passion and purpose. Together, we are striving to create ripples of positive change, leaving an indelible mark on the global community. The solution lies in transformative strategies that redefine the narrative of environmental initiatives, inspiring a collective commitment to a sustainable future!

Non-Profit.name: The Know
Non-Profit.tagline: Australian Emerging Drug Information & Resources Hub
Non-Profit.description:
The Know — NCCRED PRN. Brand Visualisation. Australian Emerging Drug Information & Resources Hub. Recreational drug use is common practice worldwide. With various ‘illicit’ drugs becoming easier to access and, in some cases, decriminalised, their usage is continuing to rise. With this comes rising cases of drug overdose, potential poisoning and long term harm to users’ health. Incidents of such harm resulting from recreational use or heavy usage can be mitigated, and even avoided entirely, if information is readily available on drugs’ safety. This is the founding mission of NCCRED’s Prompt Response Network and their newly crafted online platform ‘The Know’. Designed to provide free, up-to-date and judgement-free advice or alerts about the harm factor or legitimacy of current drug strains in the community, The Know will inform users of toxic chemicals and cases of lacing or the illegitimacy of emerging illicit drugs. Through their Prompt Response Network (PRN), NCCRED runs several programs related to emerging drugs. Their programs deliver harm reduction services, helping to develop nuanced understandings around emerging drugs (and drugs in general) used among our communities, and empowering the people affected, and the general public, with relevant information through alerts.

Challenge: Worldwide, incidents of drug abuse and drug-related accidents are increasing as people experiment with emerging drugs and the strengths increase of ‘old-school’ drugs. Such harms can be prevented and reduced by the timely sharing of accurate, relevant information. TOAST was approached by NCCRED’s PRN platform to assess this situation, looking at how information can be made accessible and clearly understood whilst remaining accurate for all Australian communities. In this vein, our team was engaged to strategise, design and launch a public-facing brand which will act as a trusted and highly reliable source of information to help reduce harm across the drug landscape in Australia. From the outset of this project, we recognised that reduction of drug use was not PRN’s core goal. Their goal was to provide accurate and up-to-date information to reduce the negative consequences that arise from drug misinformation and the consumption of compromised strains. The brand’s core purpose was to shift the narrative on drugs; supportive and open-minded values needed to be at the heart of the messaging. TOAST needed to create an altruistic brand which can be trusted. Our challenge was around building an influential platform which would be successful in engaging diverse audience groups on such a critical matter.

Solution: PRN exists to improve the health and wellbeing of Australians who partake in recreational or heavy drug use, aiming to prevent and minimise drug-related harm. Developed by a network of mixed contributors, including people who use drugs, bystanders, government bodies, and medical organisations, their new service provides access to a unique, accurate and timely source of information on emerging drugs and safe drug use. To create a brand platform that is relevant, recognisable and ownable by PRN, TOAST delved deep into their space, interviewing a vast array of community groups, from recreational drug users, sober ex-users and festival attendees, to policy makers, GPs and coroners. It was paramount that our branding resonated across multiple targets, peak bodies and locations. Having myriad audiences, our team needed to formulate a broad yet targeted brand approach, one that is flexible and provides user-centric information. PRN’s overall focus on harm reduction respects that you can use drugs and reduce potential harm, without abstinence. They are there to support and assist, not punish. A ‘people first attitude’ is core to their DNA and needed to be central to their new service’s brand footprint. Building on this, we crafted their brand and communications suite to be judgement-free - focusing solely on awareness, education, and respect. TOAST crafted a brand platform that is for people who actively use drugs, for the general public, and for professionals. Allowing drug safety information to be accessible by users, relatives and the general public, whilst also delivering a platform for the police, coroners and GPs which consolidates information to aid in policy making, trials or clinical studies. The visual identity was strongly based on insights from our qualitative user testing and interview process, wherein preferences arose for a design that did not induce shame or embarrassment and used clean layouts to allow for information to be easily understood. Logotype preferences were for a word that was simple and memorable, connoting “information sharing” or “harm reduction,” paired with a realistic, trustworthy image. Common Cause Australia’s ‘Drug Stigma Message Guide’ declared that “messages based around altruistic and community-oriented values including honesty, helpfulness and equality, were significantly more effective at activating supportive attitudes in persuadable audiences than purely fact-based messages.” Insights which led to our big idea ‘Keeping you in the know,’ which was subsequently moulded for the platform’s name ‘The Know.’ ‘Keeping (users) in the know’ is about keeping them informed and mindful, providing knowledge on dangerous drug strains and more broadly on the side effects of recreational or recurrent drug usage. Users are kept in the know through having access to accurate, comprehensive and timely information which can save lives. Beyond their pill imagery, the connected circles within The Know’s logotype are founded on a conceptual framework underpinned by community connection, collaboration and support, and the colour-blocked design highlighting ‘now’ in a contrasting orange reflects the urgency, accuracy and immediacy of their services. The primary colour palette of Purple, Orange and Green is deliberately dissimilar to the typical blue of medical and law enforcement industries to create a safe space that is not connected with punishment or pain - building on the ‘judgement-free’ aspect of their brand narrative - with purple, orange and green chosen specifically for their symbolism of wisdom, change and growth, respectively. TOAST developed this brand identity across The Know’s corporate presence, creating a cohesive brand suite and initial social media Look & Feel. Working in such a sensitive, and dangerous, environment, we focused deeply on the human-to-human dynamic of our brand design. Paying close attention to our use of language and imagery to not induce shame or create further stigma through our discourse. The Know connects individuals with the information to make safer choices, providing inspiration, knowledge and an action plan for improving individual and societal health outcomes, and saving lives.

Non-Profit.name: Juror
Non-Profit.description: Juror. NSW Department of Justice. Observe Listen Decide. The NSW Government's Department of Justice orchestrates the state's compulsory jury service. Juries are used to ensure that legal verdicts are impartial and in line with community standards of behaviour. Serving as a juror is a mandatory role, providing unique insights into the NSW court process. Juries are used in the NSW District Court and NSW Supreme Court to determine criminal and civil matters. People aged over 18 are summoned and subsequently randomly selected to serve on a jury in a particular trial. The process of collating, storing and selecting names of all eligible jurors is a large task which occurs year-round. TOAST was engaged to assist with the ideation and design of an updated user interface and communications platform which simplifies the process on both the distribution and client end. Challenge: The juror selection process is a key part of the Australian justice system. Every year, the names of approximately 200,000 potential jurors are randomly selected from the NSW Electoral Roll and included on the jury list. From this number, up to 150,000 people will be summoned to present to court, with a subsequent 9,000 being selected to fulfil their service on a jury panel. TOAST was tasked with renewing a user management system to reduce the bulk of content and business hours required to orchestrate the juror selection process. Given the evidenced high amount of data being dealt with in the NSW Department of Justice, TOAST worked to strengthen the brand and streamline their processes, aiming to reduce pain points and simplify processes for both the distribution teams and summoned jurors. Solution: TOAST designed a two-part solution with an updated User Interface Design and a Communications Suite. Our team created the overall design for the Department of Justice's online portal, mobile application and management system for jurors and potential jurors, known as Juror. This Jury Management System is an updated user database storing information on NSW jurors and contains algorithms that are used to randomly select the 200,000 jurors each year from the four million-strong NSW electoral roll. With its algorithm for random selection, the system dramatically simplifies the Jury summoning process and provides efficiencies throughout the entire procedure for Jurors and Government alike. In line with this, TOAST crafted a marketing communications suite for the NSW public. Our strategy led us to develop a concept that portrayed a sense of pride and civic duty gained from participation in NSW's Jury Service. Our Big Idea came down to the three verbs "Observe, Listen, Decide." This slogan works hand-in-hand with the authentic imagery, showcasing real people across NSW to portray a sense of ownership, responsibility and recognition for the cause. At the 2017 Sydney Design Awards, TOAST received a Gold Award in the Government Service category for our Juror campaign on behalf of the Department of Justice.

Non-Profit.name: Innovate to Regenerate
Non-Profit.description: Innovate to Regenerate. WWF Australia. Campaign Strategy & Messaging. It's Up to You. WWF have been a leading voice for conservation, regeneration and environmental protection for over half a century. They are present in over 100 countries and have the help of 5 million supporters, and growing. Partnering with businesses, individuals and the community, WWF address pressing environmental issues that can be fixed through collaborative action. They spread messages of positive, community action to ensure our planet is cared for and protected for years to come. Innovate to Regenerate is about finding innovative solutions to regenerate and future-proof Australia’s precious natural environment and communities. Challenge: Looking back across just one generation, we have experienced remarkable weather events which have undeniably changed the Australian environment. Through these repeated shared experiences, we have gained an understanding that we can do more to protect our world when we are connected with nature. WWF attest that regenerative development is what can actively reverse environmental degradation, creating a positive impact for people and the planet. TOAST was tasked with redefining this WWF message to engage wider audiences, in the hope that WWF’s initiative has a larger reach and therefore a more positive outcome for our shared natural environment. Solution: To reach the appropriate brand solution to WWF’s initiative, TOAST refocused on their key organisational outputs, their existing audience and the opportunities available to them. Our team looked to redefine their strategic angle, focusing on their longstanding message of collective community action. WWF call on the government and business stakeholders to reach a platform where their messages can be heard by the masses. But, why wait? On our own, we too can make a statement. It’s never too late to take action into our own hands. It’s in the hands and interest of everyone to create a future in which people and nature live in harmony. And if not now, when? If not you, who? Ultimately; It’s Up To Us. It’s Up To You.

Non-Profit.name: The Salvation Army
Non-Profit.description: The Salvation Army. Brand Transformation / Campaign Activation. The Freedom Partnership. Together with The Salvation Army, TOAST devised a campaign to educate, raise public awareness and empower those affected by modern slavery within Australia today. Slavery in Australia comes in many forms including trafficking, forced labour, abusive living and working conditions, isolation, violence, psychological and sexual abuse. It is often hidden and goes unreported despite being a serious crime affecting the lives of thousands. Challenge: A social media campaign was implemented using an animated project video EDM, which prompts the viewer to show support by ‘Making The Pledge’ and ‘Joining The Chain of Good’. The two-year awareness campaign also aims to extend its impact and engagement by leveraging social media communities on Facebook and Twitter. Solution: ‘The Freedom Pledge’ is a striking and bold campaign utilising an ancient symbol of law and justice, slavery and captivity known as ‘Epa’. The symbol reminds offenders of the uncompromising nature of the law and discourages all forms of slavery. This iconic symbol acts as the primary brand asset for the ‘Ending Modern Slavery’ campaign across all channels.

Non-Profit.name: MECLA
Non-Profit.description: MECLA. NSW Govt, WWF, Lendlease & Presync. Brand Activation. Game Changer Leadership. Materials Embodied Carbon Leaders’ Alliance (MECLA) is an association of leaders in the building & construction industry, government bodies and not-for-profit organisations who are committed to improving the procurement, supply chain and use of materials that cause harm to the environment. The core members of MECLA, NSW Government, WWF-Australia, Lendlease & Presync, came together with the belief that Australia can tackle the climate change threat and aligned with the Paris Agreement targets if we help transform the building and construction industry. Challenge: The built environment sector is responsible for one-quarter of Australia’s emissions. The majority of these emissions (at least 40%) occur from the embodied or upfront carbon of the materials used in building and construction in particular, steel, cement, concrete and aluminium representing over 9% of global emissions. TOAST was briefed to create a strategic positioning and brand identity to engage multiple stakeholders involved in the construction industry and rally them towards a common goal of creating a better future for Australia. The new MECLA brand needed to inspire radical collaboration, provide guidance to all market players, facilitate knowledge sharing and the uptake of low/zero-carbon materials. Solution: TOAST delved into the reason for why MECLA exists, the values that drive the organisation, and how it could be translated into a visionary brand by creating a strong strategic framework. Based on its research and the insights derived through the interviews with multiple stakeholders, TOAST created a well thought out strategic platform for the organisation: “Game Changer Leadership”, focusing on the central belief that “We are the change needed to reach net-zero emissions”. The logo and the overall brand identity created by TOAST explores the unified action of the different sectors in the construction industry; it demonstrates the intention of the organisation, with the central diamond representing a perfect collaboration between all entities' purity and a brighter future. It signifies the collaborative efforts to tackle this complex issue, the integrity to work in an ethical manner, the transparency to share knowledge and expertise, and the opportunity to move towards a zero-carbon economy future, positioning Australia in the top 5 zero-carbon materials suppliers.

Non-Profit.name: Anglicare
Non-Profit.description: Project Branding & Activation. Seed Your Future. Anglicare has long strived to discover and implement new services, initiatives and projects, establishing themselves as a service provider who is able to help people from all walks of life (e.g. newly launched Bushfire Relief Efforts). The not-for-profit organisation saw an opportunity to operate in Affordable Housing as there's an urgent need for Australian communities: Expected waiting times for Social Housing applicants in areas such as Liverpool is between 5 - 10 years. Anglicare Australia research found that for single pensioners, only three percent of available rentals were affordable. The project's unique characteristics present an attractive market proposition: Anglicare acquired three sites on which they would build properties, providing affordable housing, in addition to a small selection of strata units that act as an entry point to the market; this initiative was a direct extension of Anglicare's three core pillars: Centred in Christ, Serving customers, and Strengthening community. Whilst they may be new to the product, Anglicare's long history of serving the community and assisting those in need gives them the credibility required to make this initiative a success. "Seed your future". Challenge: A few critical threats were identified and needed to be overcome. The first one was the fact that Anglicare, whilst they were operating as a developer, didn't want to be perceived as a property developer which wanted to make money from a market opportunity; the offer would have to be well explained, and market education of the market would need to be considered. Furthermore, affordable housing carries a lot of stigma which needs to be addressed by demonstrating the overall benefits of such a program to the future residents, to the people living around them and to the broader community. Launching a brand which would encapsulate the offering without compromising Anglicare's brand footprint and would work across three different buildings was about achieving the 3 key objectives: Understand the characteristics of suburbs and potential prospects, as each market had their specifics (integrating the fact that living in a 'charity building' is a perception that neither SAHF nor strata residents wish to portray); Protect Anglicare's existing brand equity (avoid being perceived as a profit-generating property developer); Sell units in a unique product offering (The product type means purchasers will predominantly be owner occupiers (FHB, upgraders and downsizers) although investors may show growing interest based on favourable market conditions). Solution: From a comprehensive strategic framework including research, interviews and workshop, TOAST was able to articulate a unique strong idea: present the act of living in such a place as a great new chapter in life. We unravelled the product proposition thinking the new apartment developments would present the beginning of a new stage in people's lives: A new home; the habitat for a new chapter in life; A new building to enjoy a good quality of life; A new environment with like-minded people; A new day-to-day life from now onwards; A new opportunity to shape their future; A future with Anglicare commitment for 25 years; A relevant platform for Anglicare for years to come. With this idea, we believed the 3 programs will offer the opportunity for people to have new hope, a fresh new start in life; a concept was born: Seed Your Future. We wanted to articulate the positive outcome to enrich people's lives, while creating a concept that works for everyone: affordable housing tenants, investors, future renters, owner occupiers, broader community and Anglicare's key stakeholders and partners. "Seed your future" is the start of a new cycle in life. We chose to illustrate this idea through symbolic native Australian plants, drawing similarities between the life cycle of people with life cycles in nature. Within this big idea, each building would have a name born from an Australian native plant, a full marketing suite including digital experience, a multidimensional concept delivering positive outcomes for all audiences. In collaboration with the appointed real estate agency McGrath, the campaign was a full success to attract interest from local buyers, as long as proper communication processes and collateral was established.

Non-Profit.name: City of Ryde
Non-Profit.description: Site Activation/ Brand Engagement. Ryde Here, Ryde Now. The City of Ryde is the council which holds jurisdiction over the Ryde LGA. Their youth division is oriented towards 12 - 24-year-olds who work, live, study or play within the region, and offer a range of programs (of varying commitment) all aimed at helping the LGA's young individuals to grow and develop. Challenge: Whilst the City of Ryde's youth programs offer a variety of valuable experiences to prospective participants, the number of young people who actually engage with the offerings was far too low. Ryde city council needed to pivot their youth brand to drive engagement in local discussions and connect with the younger demographic. Thus, the City of Ryde's youth brand needed to be addressed and re-engineered from the ground up, to help more effectively communicate its value proposition. Solution: Through a series of interviews and community engagement, TOAST uncovered that the Youth were seeking much more than recreational fun and social media recognition. They live in the moment, and possess a strong commitment to tackling today's societal and environmental challenges, pushing away the stigma that they are the future. They share common beliefs based on a sense of urgency to be heard and to act now. Our workshop process allowed us to define the organisation's core identity and the findings to create the name and visual look and feel that will eventually inspire the Youth Initiatives logo. The brand needed to mirror that the youth community is actively seeking opportunities to make a genuine impact and to obtain the skills they'd need to become the leaders of not just tomorrow, but today. This led to the development of a range of new community programs promoted through the strategic positioning of 'Ryde here, Ryde now' and a unique look and feel connected with our audiences, based on playful brand narratives and icons. This positioning was rolled out across a series of communications, shining a light on the programs which supported the needs of the youth community of Ryde.

Non-Profit.name: Black Dog Institute
Non-Profit.description: Brand Transformation. For a Mentally Healthier World. The Black Dog Institute is a not-for-profit facility for diagnosis, treatment and prevention of mood disorders such as depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. Since their foundation in 1985 as the 'Mood Disorders Unit' at Prince Henry Hospital, Sydney, they have been at the forefront of mental health research. Their work in mood disorders keeps evolving through their investigation of new and better ways to treat and prevent conditions like anxiety and depression through better marketing and communication, digital tools and novel treatments, impacting nationally and internationally with major initiatives including prevention campaigns. Challenge: 1 in 5 Australians will experience symptoms of mental illness in any given year. That's around 5 million people. And roughly 60% of these people won't seek help. As the only medical research institute in Australia to investigate mental health across our lifespan, Black Dog aims to create a mentally healthier world for everyone. They had a clearly articulated vision for a mentally healthier world, however they felt the brand was not reflecting their ethos and not explaining enough about how their work is impacting Australians' mental health and the support they provide to people in need. TOAST needed to give their brand a youthful refresh which will be more closely aligned with their mission and help engage discussion with people dealing with mental health issues. Also, it was critical for the branding to be strong while making Black Dog highly accessible to a range of audiences (particularly young First Nations people). Solution: TOAST undertook extensive research and through a branding workshop developed a more streamlined, concise branding suite using the organisation's core values and colour palette. First, we needed to understand how Black Dog's 'translational' research works and helps discover new solutions, fosters connections and enables the institute to drive evidence-informed change around mental health where it's needed most. A communication strategy was then developed redefining the brand language and visual assets, providing Black Dog with highly adaptive, reusable logos, imagery and messaging to generate engagement from multiple audiences, at multiple levels. The result is a more clear, concise brand that speaks across multiple platforms to bring the topic of mental health to the forefront. Our strategic framework drove the name and design of a new brand, high in symbolism; Black Dog refers to Winston Churchill's term to describe his own depression. His famous victory symbol and the dog's shadow pay respect to the fact that mental illness can be ever present, however it is not the definition of any individual. It is a fine balance and personal duality with two parts talking to each other: Winston Churchill's famous victory peace sign represents the positivity of overcoming (hope); In the shade, a reference to his depression as his "Black Dog"; meaning that for someone living with a mental illness, it can shadow them, even in victory. The project was awarded Gold at the 2018 Sydney Design Awards in the Service - Community category.

Non-Profit.name: Renewable Recovery
Non-Profit.tagline: Clean Energy is not the Future...It's the Now!
Non-Profit.description: WWF Australia. Campaign Development. Clean Energy is not the Future...It's the Now! As the world shifts to a low carbon future, Australia has everything we need to take the lead and become a renewable energy export superpower. We've got endless sunshine, plenty of space, powerful winds, world-class expertise and strong trade relationships: it's a winning combination. The twin crises of the 2019/2020 bushfires and the Covid-19 pandemic have created a need for a recovery package that helps the country rebuild. WWF-Australia is calling on our leaders to make Australia the world's leading exporter of renewable energy by 2030. Challenge: In September 2020, WWF flagged the fact that there was a critical opportunity before the delivery of the next Federal budget to see the work commence, through the delivery of a renewable recovery stimulus package. WWF-Australia believes that renewable energy should be a major focus of stimulus investment, and we have specific projects in mind. But, to secure that stimulus investment, we need to change the thinking within bureaucracy and government. TOAST's challenge was to convince key decision-makers that a clean energy stimulus was the best way to accelerate Australia's economic recovery. The campaign required bipartisan appeal in order to change the minds of detractors and secure our nation's future. Solution: WWF-Australia planned a print-driven advocacy campaign, with the centrepiece being a 'wrap' of the Canberra edition of The Australian masthead. Our central insight was to challenge people's initial perceptions surrounding renewable energy, allowing them to actively engage in a new conversation. By grabbing the attention with a challenging message while telling the story of what's possible through an investment in renewable stimulus, we wanted to secure significant government investment in 5-6 key initiatives proposed by WWF-Australia. To cut through, we decided rather than starting our communications with the traditional renewable communications format, we could take the opposite stance to drive engagement. Framing the role of renewables as a tool for job creation and using the language of big businesses to explain the benefits. The campaign's seemingly anti-renewables hook 'Clean Energy is Not the Future' and black & white colour scheme draw the attention of audiences, before subverting their expectations and emphasising the campaign's true positioning - 'It's the NOW!' The 'wrap' of The Australian newspaper distils the dense, technical text contained within WWF-Australia's reports into its most concise and interesting form, including infographics, quotes, and key stats. TOAST's strategic communications helped WWF-Australia's advocacy campaign to win the attention of Federal and State Government policymakers. The organisation received numerous invitations to discuss its proposed stimulus after the launch of its media campaign. These meetings created tangible outcomes, including a federal commitment to invest over $140million in a hydrogen export hub, renewable and battery storage microgrids, and programs to support community organisations to lower their energy bills. TOAST is immensely proud to have created an impactful campaign on behalf of an organisation seeking to create a better present and future for all Australians.

Property.name: Matched
Property.description: Matched. Property that Puts People First. Matching People to Property. Matched are a buyer's agency that do things differently. Instead of pursuing profits, they prioritise people, combining empathy and strategy to find the place that fits buyers perfectly. To launch their start-up on the Sydney market and appeal to buyers of all shapes and sizes, they turned to TOAST. Sectors: Property. Services: Brand Positioning, Unique Value Proposition, Service Positioning, Brand Architecture, Brand Territory, Visual Identity, Tone of Voice, Brand Guidelines, Stationery, Out-of-home, Social Media Kit, UX/UI, Web Design. Challenge: Buyer's agencies are all-too-common, but not all of them are made equal. They were originally created to represent the buyer (and not the seller) in real estate deals, but it hasn't quite panned out that way. Recently, inexperienced players and flashy social personalities have crept into the market. They often make grand promises, but deliver not-so-grand results, lacking the hard-won knowledge to find the right place for their buyers. Unsurprisingly, this has weakened trust in the category and made buyers wary of new agencies who may not have their best interests at heart. Solution: To succeed, Matched needed to strike a different tone, one that's less transactional and more personal. We framed them as the agency that takes a tailored approach to property, matching people to the place that's right for them (and only them). To capture the meticulous care and expertise they deliver throughout the process, we developed The Matched Experience methodology. It shows how Matched get to know the buyer's hopes, dreams, likes and dislikes, before pinpointing a property that ticks all the boxes, be that on a personal, financial, emotional or legal level. Connecting all the pieces of the brand was the puzzle logo, a simple but charming symbol of Matched's personalised process. Blending an upbeat Green Lime with a trustworthy Deep Blue, it served as a flexible device that slotted into a range of brand applications, from highlighting stunning homes on their website, to showcasing the perfect matches they'd delivered for their clients. We then added real buyers into the mix, with photography that captures the genuine emotions people feel when they've finally found the right place: joy, satisfaction, calm, excitement, even relief after months of searching, stressing and getting nowhere. By presenting Matched as a truly trustworthy partner, the brand can appeal to a generation of buyers who are sick of the games, dead ends and empty promises, opening the door to more clients, more success and more perfect matches.

Property.name: Goodspace
Property.tagline: A Workspace that Keeps Up with its Workers
Property.description: Goodspace. Sentumar. Brand Transformation. A Workspace that Keeps Up with its Worker. Sentumar Becomes Goodspace. Sentumar wanted to get more entrepreneurs hustling, collaborating and thriving in their exceptionally versatile workplaces. Sectors: Property, Corporate. Services: Brand Positioning, Unique Value Proposition, Service Positioning, Brand Architecture, Brand Territory, Visual Identity, Brand Essence, Tone of Voice, Brand Guidelines, Stationery, Big Idea, Illustration. Challenge: Entrepreneurs' businesses move as fast as they do. One week, they might need a room to take calls in. The next, a meeting space to pitch to clients in. The next, a full-blown office teeming with fresh hires. The week after that, a showroom for their shiny new products. The week after that, a warehouse to ship their stock to the world. Their needs can change in the blink of an ROI. But unfortunately, most workspace providers can't keep up. Usually, they offer one kind of office space that can't grow with founders' businesses, limiting what they can do, who they can work with and where they can go. Solution: Sentumar won't hold you back. They offer a range of workspaces in one place. Co-working rooms, e-comm hubs, full office floors, warehousing, dispatching, event spaces, photography studios, even podcast rooms... This near-limitless range of spaces unlocks near-limitless possibilities. All of a sudden, entrepreneurs have the space they need to do whatever their business requires and grow faster. We saw the opportunity right away and positioned Sentumar as "Flexible spaces where good things happen". Laser-focused on hungry young business, it reflects how Sentumar provides a breadth of spaces that can scale with anyone's ambition. Good Name - To appeal to our audience's need to succeed, we renamed Sentumar "Goodspace". Simple, informal, punchy, it spoke the language of success with charm and gusto. Good Illustrations - We filled their office walls with kaleidoscopic and inspiring doodles that capture the endless possibilities their offices support. Good Visuals - We used bold type, upbeat photography and a vibrant colour palette, nodding to that "sky's-the-limit" feeling of running a growing business. Results: Good things are now happening for Goodspace, too. People are flocking to their hubs, the business is growing all the time, and they've opened up in three new locations. Just as they help entrepreneurs thrive, we've helped them do exactly the same. Good stuff.

Property.name: Willow
Property.description: Willow. Sekisui House. Sanctuary - Stage Three. Immerse Yourself in Nature. Nestled on the water's edge in Wentworth Point, Sekisui House's masterplan community 'Sanctuary' presents a dynamic lifestyle that intertwines people, culture, and the natural environment. Building on the great success of Stage 2 of Sanctuary comprising Laguna, Glade & Revive, the project has advanced gracefully into its third stage, 'Willow'. Overlooking the Parramatta River and bordering the masterplan's neighbourhood green, Stage 3 is beautifully located within national parkland, offering breathtaking river and city views. Willow, sequestered in this serene site, features a holistic design that includes a private lagoon pool and meticulously curated podium gardens, providing an exclusive oasis for Stage 3 residents. Willow comprises 323 premium waterside apartments centred around lush open spaces, achieving perfect harmony with nature. These residences are elegantly designed to facilitate an inside-out connection between landscape and architecture, embracing the tranquil, curious flow of the Parramatta River and the highest international living standards. This development seamlessly integrates the surrounding natural landscape with modern architecture, offering a unique and harmonious living experience. Sectors: Property, Luxury, Lifestyle. Services: Place Visioning, Brand Architecture, Brand Positioning, Brand Territory, Brand Visualisation, Editorial Design, Marketing, Motion Graphics, Naming, UX/UI, Web Design, Video Production. Challenge: Having worked with Sekisui House from the inception of Sanctuary's Place Vision, our TOASTies were excited to embark on Stage 3's campaign; as a staged addition in a large-scale masterplan, it was imperative that the Sanctuary property branding and strategic vision remained as the common thread that ties all elements together. Harmony, vibrancy, a sense of calm, and livability are fundamental attributes defining a sanctuary and are wonderfully evident across the Stage 3 development. The Willow residences bring newfound energy and life to the Sanctuary precinct. Aligned and connected with the overall branding and message of Sanctuary's masterplan, these buildings have an infectious spirit. Stage 3, nestled in a lush parkland setting, acts as a natural refuge with its unobstructed views and unrivalled access to nature. As an element within the Sanctuary masterplan brand, Willow is identifiable by the unique kaleidoscopic logotype. In creating this gracefully fragmented circular imagery, TOAST was inspired by the fundamental principles within Japanese design, such as simplicity, understated beauty, and tranquillity. It's an intricate but elegant wreath, a symbol that ties all elements of Sanctuary together. Solution: Set back from the water and surrounded by wild parklands, Willow leverages the verdant energy of parkside life. For Stage 3 in Sanctuary's development, TOAST created the tagline 'Immerse Yourself in Nature,' showcasing Willow as the incomparable green heart of Sanctuary and harnessing Sekisui House's principle of 'Satoyama,' to create harmony between humans and nature. Across Willow, nature acts as a bridge between the apartments and the wider landscape, creating an unrivalled living experience where nature and urban living seamlessly integrate. The harmony and communication between our inside and outside worlds are fundamental elements within Sanctuary's brand footprint, making this masterplan evermore unique. Willow's logo was thus inspired by its 47+ hectares of verdant surrounding parklands. Bejewelled by vibrant greens to suggest a life surrounded by the lush, expansive landscape to explore, Willow's logotype and stage identity lives in proud connection to the land. Stage 3, as the absolute green heart of Sanctuary, delivers a beautifully unique experience for residents and the wider community. Spaces that are in harmony with nature and abundant in vibrant interactions epitomise comfortable living and offer a fulfilled life experience.

Property.name: Rethink Group
Property.description: Rethink Group. Brand Transformation. Wealth of Ideas. At TOAST, we recently had the privilege of working with premium property investment firm, Rethink Investing. Founded by Scott O'Neill in 2009 and based in Bondi Junction, they have created a leading name for themselves in the property investing realm. The company distinguished itself in the early days by focusing on cash-flow-positive commercial properties in high-growth areas, diverging from the conventional focus on residential investments. This success laid the groundwork for the new, consolidated corporate brand 'Rethink Group,' which now includes multiple verticals such as Rethink Financing, Rethink Residential Investing & Rethink Property Lawyers. It was the creation of this group branding approach that TOAST was engaged to establish and lay the foundation for. Sectors: Corporate, Luxury, Property, Finance. Services: Brand Architecture, Brand Strategy, Brand Positioning, Unique Value Proposition, Service Positioning, Brand Territory, Visual Identity, Brand Essence, Tone of Voice, Brand Guidelines, Stationery, Motion Graphics, UX/UI, Web Design. Challenge: Rethink Investing approached our team at the end of 2023 with a significant challenge: to create an overarching Group brand that would unify their diverse vertical businesses while maintaining their unique identities. They needed a cohesive brand architecture that reflected their rapid growth and industry success, ensuring a consistent and professional image that would resonate with their high-end clients. Solution: Our team of Toasties embarked on a comprehensive strategic roadmap for Rethink Group, initiating the process with extensive research, analysis and numerous stakeholder interviews. This approach allowed us to deeply understand the unique qualities and market positions of each vertical business within the Group. Collaborating closely with Rethink Group's leadership and marketing teams, we developed a brand strategy that highlighted their core values, strengths, and collective vision for the future. A central element of the new brand identity for Rethink Group was the tagline, "Wealth of Ideas," an evolution of their core DNA, "Wealth Creators Through Property," devised in our stakeholder strategy session. This tagline encapsulates Rethink Group's dedication to empowering financial journeys through unique and forward-thinking property investment services. It also offers extensive flexibility, allowing for variations such as "Wealth of Opportunities," "Wealth of Experience," and "Wealth of Knowledge," tailored to different audiences and contexts. Building on this brand narrative of "Wealth of Ideas" we created a 'house of brands' company architecture, enabling each vertical to retain its distinct identity while aligning under the unified Rethink Group umbrella. Our design team crafted a versatile and cohesive visual identity system, including logos, colour schemes, and typography that differentiated each business while maintaining visual coherence. We delivered a comprehensive brand guidelines document with specifications for each vertical, ensuring consistency across all touchpoints. These final designs and colour palettes played a crucial role in conveying each brand's values and the new image of Rethink Group. The primary Rethink Group logotype is an elegant evolution of their original keyhole icon. Our team enhanced its design, reflecting the known 'R' of Rethink in a bespoke style that embodies the dedication and unwavering ingenuity underpinning the brand. This design echoes the values of authenticity, empowerment, excellence, and disruption, setting Rethink apart as a true industry leader. The conceptual framework behind the Rethink Group logotype captures the brand's core values, creating an ownable icon that champions their legacy while elevating it to the highly respectable status it has achieved to date. The Rethink Group corporate colour palette features luxurious tones of navy and champagne, with varying hues indicating the quality, expertise and dedication that underpin the brand. These colours were carefully chosen to reflect the sophistication and premium nature of the Group's offerings. Staying within the elegant, luxurious territory of the Group brand, the palette is slightly tweaked throughout the verticals to create individual identities for each brand while simultaneously setting them apart and uniting them with the overall company. Result: The result of our collaboration was a refined, professional brand identity for Rethink Group that effectively represents their expansive portfolio and industry leadership. This new brand architecture not only unified their vertical businesses but also positioned them for continued growth and success in the competitive property investment landscape.

Property.name: Bowerbird
Property.description: Bowerbird — Brand Transformation. The Art of Connecting. Crafting the Perfect First Impression. When it comes to property, you only get one chance to make the right first impression. And in the Australian market, where standards are high and competition is intense, every detail matters. From commercial to residential, Bowerbird is an interior design and property styling team that excels at connecting people and place. They've grown quickly by creating success where it matters: curating environments that set the stage for great experiences, and ultimately, great results. As futuremakers, we were asked to support Bowerbird in shaping the brand's next chapter, presenting their offering to the market in a way that hits exactly the right note. Challenge: Right from the outset, it was clear they were all about artistry. Through their unique mix of creativity, passion, expertise and dedication, they can see the full potential of a space, and bring that out through their designs. But they're not just about stunning spaces. They think hard about the functionality of the location, so that it can meet the needs of whoever's living, socialising or working in it, be they a tenant, colleague or customer. In this way, they blend form and function across everything they make. The challenge, then, was to build a brand positioning and identity that married the aesthetic with the strategic; the creative flair with outcomes that create value for their clients, owners and residents. And in a category defined by minimalist branding with little cut-through, the design needed to have more personality, while maintaining the sophistication needed to appeal to clients across a broad range of categories. If that balance was off even a little, potential clients would switch off and move on. Solution: We built a brand that focused on creating a connection between people and place. On a creative level, they connect people to beautiful spaces and design features, so that they can admire them, appreciate them and enjoy them. And on a strategic level, those spaces connect people to each other, so they can live or work to their full potential. In this way, their brand footprint is centered "value creation" in the fullest sense of the word, turning their labour and resources into something that meets the needs of others both aesthetically and functionally. This creative idea translated to a brand identity; a visual territory which celebrates curation and collection, supported by the tagline 'The Art of Connecting'. At its heart was the 'BB' monogram, a seal of quality, taste and also character, without limiting the brand to a particular style or territory. A flexible colour system (revolving around a signature dusty blue) was introduced, allowing the brand to sub-brand their whole suite of services – from private residential and commercial residential to special projects. The Result: With a brand identity that emphasises the connection of ideas, people and places without boundaries, anything is now possible for Bowerbird. By elevating their brand so it's both creatively appealing and commercially compelling, Bowerbird has the identity it needs to secure new clients, expand their business and, ultimately, meet the high expectations of the Australian property market during that crucial first call, pitch or meeting. Because branding isn't just about building the right identity. It's about striking the right impression, too.

Property.name: Calico Marina
Property.description: Calico Marina — Place Visioning. The Place to Be. Located in the pristine waters of Port Hacking River, Calico Marina is a destination of seaside bliss boasting stunning beaches, tidal rock pools and incredible sunset viewpoints. A renewal of this underused side of Cronulla - Calico is a perfectly positioned destination for a sunny day, afternoon and evening by the water. A serene beachside location and community hub bustling with the daily marina activity, the creative vision behind this marina's uplift was for a place of connection, celebration and exclusivity; the place to be in Cronulla. Challenge: The rise in desirability for a coastal lifestyle positions Cronulla as a thriving cosmopolitan area and an increasingly sought-after destination to live and work. This luxe marina destination is built with precision and beautiful functionality; the curvature of the architecture mimicking the coastal grace of its natural setting. This revitalised waterfront precinct integrates luxury that redefines Cronulla. Becoming the main attraction of this previously underused bayside region, the place narrative required the area to be painted as an exclusive opportunity - a unique destination on the water. The overall brand footprint and strategic vision for this site thus needed to encapsulate its natural beauty and deluxe allure, whilst recognising its historical functionality as a marina. Solution: Building on knowledge gleaned from benchmark analyses, our team recognised that successful marinas go beyond their functional purpose. They are destinations in their own right; surrounded by buzzing restaurants, bars and clubs, they are key local access points to the region all wrapped in an air of sophistication. To create this sophisticated site, we capitalised on the marina's neighbouring unrivalled area of Gunnamatta Bay. TOAST looked into the history and usage of this site and in doing so discovered the meaning for Cronulla, or 'Kurranulla' in the local Gweagal dialect, as 'place of the pink seashells'. This became key to the place narrative and led to the name generation of 'Calico', derived from the sleek pink Calico Scallop seashell. Being unique, eye-catching and inspiring, this name mirrors the curved shell-like architectural form of the precinct design whilst beautifully linking with the area's indigenous history. Our strategic brand positioning thus connects community, a coastal lifestyle and innovative design by creating an iconic marina; a true destination reimagining hospitality and engaging the senses. Harmonising a beachside lifestyle with contemporary design, Calico Marina oozes lavish opulence with a laid-back coastal air to deliver a unique destination for all to indulge. Without losing its functional purpose, this is a luxe waterfront destination which enriches daily lives today and into the future; an indulgent place for socialising and celebrating, for love, fun and community connection. With Calico's intrinsic feel of exclusivity, it is more than a destination; a strong statement in the Cronulla landscape, Calico Marina is a game-changer destination.

Property.name: Sekisui House
Property.description: Sekisui House — Advancing Sekisui House's brand impact within Australia. Here for better. Since 2016, TOAST has partnered with global property leader Sekisui House, the world's largest residential developer and a benchmark for sustainable living. What began as a single engagement has grown into a long-term collaboration built on shared ambition, integrity and an obsession with craft. Together, we've helped redefine how a property brand can look, feel and behave in the Australian market. Challenge: Sekisui House's legacy of innovation is unmatched globally, yet in Australia the brand needed a refreshed, connected experience—one that translated its philosophy of better living into a contemporary, local context. The task was to bring clarity, cohesion and emotional resonance to a brand operating in a competitive and rapidly shifting property landscape, while honouring its deep design principles and human-centred values. Solution: TOAST worked side-by-side with Sekisui House to elevate every touchpoint of its brand experience—uniting strategy, design and storytelling into a single, purposeful narrative. This collaborative foundation ultimately led to TOAST being entrusted with full branding and marketing responsibilities for Sekisui House Australia's two newest Sydney communities in Norwest and Wentworth Point. The result is a partnership that continues to shape how Australians engage with place: thoughtful, detailed, quietly bold—and always moving toward what's next.

Property.name: Calira
Property.description: Calira — Anchor Group. Painting Properties in a Luxurious Light. Where Life Flows Naturally. Nestled near the banks of the Paramatta River, Calira is a luxury development teeming with beautiful amenities. Featuring panoramic views of the Sydney Harbour and CBD, thoughtfully crafted and expansive interiors, a landscaped rooftop wellness zone, and natural walking paths that trace the contours of the water, it has everything you need in one idyllic haven. Anchor Group, the developer of this collection of residences, approached us to create an identity that would reflect its undeniable beauty to Sydney's discerning downsizers. Challenge: The natural stone finishes. The state-of-the-art gym. The thriving local community. The flowing balconies. There were layers upon layers of features that made Calira a premium and high-end property. But in a near-flooded market, we needed to home in on the one thing that made these residences truly distinctive, the one feature that would catch the eye of buyers who had no shortage of excellent choices all over the city. We led research, workshops and collaborative discovery calls with the architect, Lewis Lau, the developer, Charbel Obeid, and the sales agent, Clayton Ross, and conducted our own in-depth site visit to the development and the surrounding urban neighbourhood. Drawing on first-hand insight and desktop research alike, we uncovered what made Calira truly luxurious and one-of-a-kind: the shimmer of the river itself. Solution: With north-facing apartments looking out onto the Paramatta River, Calira's residents are treated to the sunlight dancing on the water every sunrise and sunset, facilitating a lifestyle that's serene, glamorous and calming. This natural glimmer shone a light on the direction for the entire campaign: we gave the development the tagline "Where Life Flows Naturally" and crafted a visual identity that channelled a sense of ease, light and fluidity at every turn, with an iconic glint symbol, undulating lines and gold-tinged fonts at its heart. Campaign materials such as the EDM, website, social cutdowns and brochure then teased the glimmer from every angle: up-close, by the riverbank, from the balcony and from far, far above, while artfully highlighting all the other amenities Calira had to offer, from the interior to the wellness facilities to the surrounding lifestyle. The perfect way to paint a luxurious collection of residences in a truly luxurious light.

Property.name: Anchor Group
Property.description: Anchor Group — Elevating the Brand to Reflect the Business. The Art of Elevated Living. What do you do when your business has outgrown your brand? That was the key challenge Anchor Group came to us with. As a leading development, construction and asset management firm, they excel at designing luxury homes and commercial spaces that embody elegance, detail and distinction in Sydney's most aspirational areas. They now wanted to align the way they looked with the way they worked, so that their true philosophy could shine through everything they do. It was a textbook case of harmonising business and brand on every level. Challenge: But why are Anchor's properties so exceptional? What was the essence of the business that the new brand needed to express? Following a detailed audit of the business, the answer became unmistakably clear: Anchor Group don't just design properties to impress, but to enhance the way people live. In other words, their focus isn't just on the buildings themselves, but the lifestyles they house, shape and support. Solution: We made this distinctive approach the foundation for the brand, giving rise to a value proposition that's all about lifestyle curation: "The Art of Elevated Living". Elevated Logo: Smooth, sophisticated but also sturdy, the logo embodies the flair and practicality that defines Anchor Group. Elevated Design System: Designed not just for clarity, but also emotion, the artisanal fonts and intricate patterns reflect Anchor Group's obsessive attention to detail. Elevated Website: The art of elevated scrolling: stunning property photography, clean layouts and effortless navigation all come together to create a flawless user experience. The Results: Today, the look, feel and tone of the brand doesn't eclipse the excellent work Anchor Group does, but reflects it. With brand and business singing from the same hymn sheet, their underlying value is clear for all to see. When an elevated brand meets an elevated business, it leads to elevated results.

Property.name: Arclane
Property.description: Arclane — Brand Transformation. Makers of Modern Living. Standing Out by Standing for Artistry. Arclane are an ultra-creative, premium property developer. Like any ambitious business at the height of their craft, they were looking to strengthen their presence in the Australian property market. And they didn't just want an immediate impact or a quick win: they wanted to build a brand that would nurture steady growth for years to come. Challenge: Cutting through in the world of property is a tall order. It's a market with big players and considerable competition, each striving to be top of mind for buyers, architects and investors alike, so it's very easy to be crowded out and become invisible. But while there's no shortage of developers, there is a gap in the market: there are many formulaic, standard-issue developments out there. They tick the boxes and make commercial sense, but lack the sense of flair or beauty that make them a truly high-value property. But Arclane is different. Following a series of in-depth strategic interviews with their team, we discovered their unique value in the market: They approach every space with the care and consideration of a craftsperson, blending aesthetics and functionality to create spaces that are as beautiful as they are usable. They're places that inspire and you can admire, while still having the right features to support living, working and playing with ease. Instead of being places people just spend time in or move through, they're places people love. Solution: This insight led to our brand idea, "Makers of Modern Living". It captures how every development perfectly marries form and function, beauty and purpose, to provide a refined and modern living experience. By giving residents the best of both worlds, and standing for something more aspirational than transactional, it was a real challenge to the status quo of the market. It was then a question of applying this philosophy to everything the brand made, said and did. We created a design system that was spacious, clean and easily navigable, but with plenty of flourishes mixed in: flowing lines, elegant curves and elevated imagery, all the finishing touches that make you stop and stare. The logo then brought it all together in a symbol of incredible visual economy. "Makers of Modern Living" was etched into its very shape, with three arched versions of the letter "M" combining to create a stunning building. A true work of art, just like their developments. The Results: "Makers of Modern Living" proved to be the perfect platform for the brand. Not only is the idea distinctive in the market, it elegantly summarises what makes Arclane's developments of superior value. Which just goes to show: to avoid becoming invisible, you need to lean into your beauty.

Property.name: Rethink Website
Property.description: Rethink Website. Rethink Group. Website Transformation. Wealth of Ideas. Creating a Group Lead-Generating Digital Ecosystem. In today's digital landscape, a fragmented online presence can hinder a group's growth. At TOAST, we architect digital ecosystems that drive performance, combining strategic brand thinking, human-centred design, and results-driven UX/UI to unlock brands' full digital potential. Challenge: How can Rethink group achieve unity while allowing individual business units to maintain distinct digital identities? Our approach focused on establishing a consistent design language across all sites, developing flexible customised templates, refining the Group Brand Picture to meet each business line business requirements, enabling seamless cross-navigation, and designing conversion-optimised user journeys. Solution: We began with in-depth research to define a unified Brand Picture and UVP, conducting stakeholder interviews, user analytics, competitor analysis, and collaborative workshops. This strategic framework was then translated in an engaging brand visualisation that unified the group while preserving each vertical's unique identity. Next, we focused on user experience and interface design. By collaborating with each unit's leadership, we developed digital narratives aligning with the group's mission and individual objectives. Tailored content strategies, decision-making flows, and actionable CTAs were crafted for each vertical. Leveraging our research insights, we crafted a conversion-optimised and visually engaging digital experience. Our approach emphasised mobile-first design, visual consistency, user-centred functionality, performance optimisation, and seamless integrations to enhance marketing and operational efficiency. The Results: Each business unit now boasts a refined, results-driven digital identity. A transformation which was applied across multiple business units within the Rethink Group, including: Rethink Investing: Designed to engage investors and simplify property investment education; Rethink Financing: Connecting clients with tailored financial solutions and mortgage brokers; Rethink Commercial Education: Providing expert-led programs to educate and empower investors; Rethink Property Lawyers: Establishing a trustworthy online presence for property law services, making legal guidance more accessible; Rethink Residential: Elevating the property development experience with an engaging, high-performance digital platform; Rethink Property Insurance: Offering seamless access to property-related insurance policies through a user-friendly digital experience; Rethink Renewables: Showcasing sustainability-driven solutions with a forward-thinking digital strategy. Today, Rethink Group benefits from a cohesive, trust-building brand experience that enhances engagement and boosts lead generation.

Property.name: Perifa
Property.description: Perifa. Versatile Group. Brand Visualisation. Your Tomorrow is Our Today. Versatile, a well-established name in the construction and property sector, approached TOAST with a clear objective: to re-establish their group brand architecture and effectively separate their service offerings into distinct verticals. This strategic initiative began with the creation of the 'Perifa' brand, which would serve as the development arm of the business. The new brand would encompass three core verticals: Capital, Investments and Property. TOAST's task was to work closely with Perifa's leadership to craft a visual and strategic foundation that elevated the brand and aligned with their ambitious growth trajectory. The goal was to position Perifa as a forward-thinking, integrated solutions provider in the Australian market. Challenge: Transitioning from the legacy of Versatile, a company renowned for delivering construction, fit-out and refurbishment projects since 1974, to the newly created Perifa brand posed a unique challenge. While Versatile's heritage in the construction industry was strong, the shift to Perifa marked a pivotal moment, positioning the business as a diversified entity offering integrated solutions across Capital, Investments and Property. TOAST needed to clarify and elevate each of these verticals within the brand architecture while ensuring Perifa's overarching identity represented the company's expansive service offering. The challenge lay in creating clarity and cohesion across the newly defined verticals, while simultaneously evolving the market perception to align with Perifa's broader capabilities. TOAST's role was to ensure that Perifa's brand communicated its comprehensive value proposition to investors, clients and internal teams, highlighting its ability to deliver certainty, innovation, and end-to-end value across the entire development lifecycle. Solution: TOAST collaborated closely with Perifa's management to create a brand identity and architecture that clearly distinguished each of the group's verticals while maintaining a cohesive, unified brand presence. Starting with the foundation of Perifa, TOAST developed the strategic framework to ensure it was clearly defined and positioned as a high-calibre entity within the brand. Perifa's new tagline, "Your tomorrow is our today," encapsulates the brand's forward-thinking philosophy and underscores its role in delivering certainty and value across its diverse offerings. To visually communicate this, TOAST crafted an uber-contemporary brand identity, featuring a core metallic teal palette, accentuated by regal-toned foils to differentiate each vertical while maintaining a harmonious aesthetic across the brand. The visual language was anchored by a contemporary brand icon, combining the letter "P" with a forward-pointing arrow, symbolising Perifa's commitment to progress and innovation. This strategic brand architecture allowed Perifa to present itself as an integrated, multi-disciplined group with a strong focus on future-oriented solutions. TOAST's comprehensive rebranding for Perifa ultimately resulted in a clearly defined, elevated group structure that enhanced market perception, bolstered internal cohesion, and positioned Perifa as a leading player in property development, capital investment and construction solutions.

Property.name: 20 Martin Place
Property.description: 20 Martin Place. Pembroke. Web Transformation. A Luminous Landmark. Pembroke, an international real estate business with over twenty-five years of experience, operates from eight offices worldwide. Their thoughtful approach combines global insight and local expertise to create community-focused spaces. Pembroke's core mission is to create long-term value through this integration and a passionate real estate team. To enhance their digital presence and streamline documentation, Pembroke enlisted TOAST to revamp their website and produce a comprehensive leasing document for their new city-centre acquisition in Sydney. Our goal was to empower Pembroke to lease and sell office space more efficiently. Challenge: [no descriptive text provided]. Solution: TOAST's website redesign for Pembroke reflected the brands' leading status and cohesive team approach, along with positioning their new acquisition, 20 Martin Place, as a prestigious location, appealing to businesses seeking a prominent address with excellent access and amenities. We focused on User Experience by dividing the site into accessible segments to highlight leasing opportunities at 20 Martin Place and other properties. Implementing a robust CRM-focused solution, we customised the user database to support segmented consumer profiles for personalised engagement. Our mobile-first, responsive design ensured accessibility across all devices, providing a premium user experience. Similarly, the leasing document presented 20 Martin Place as a signature building in Sydney, known for its prime location, flexibility, and top-tier tenant amenities. The refreshed website and leasing campaign bolsters Pembroke's brand credibility establishing them as a leader in connecting buyers, sellers, investors and developers, and encourages tenants to relocate their business to Sydney's premier business address.

Property.name: Vue - Brochure
Property.description: Vue - Brochure. Sammut Group. The Perfect Blend. Sammut Group is a full-service luxury property development company. They elevate industry standards and expectations by applying principles of superior design and construction to residential, commercial, retail and hotel precincts from coast to coast. With a primary focus on strengthening their luxury property development arm and diversifying the company into other lifestyle businesses, the group is creating new standards of experiential luxury through major residential, commercial and hospitality-centred projects. This business core rings true in Vue, their latest project, an oceanview luxury mixed-use precinct in the heart of Cronulla. Offering intricately designed apartments, deluxe amenities and streetfront dining and retail, Vue, designed by PBD Architects, will be pivotal in generating economic investment in the heart of Sydney's Southern beaches. Challenge: Vue is set to be a catalyst project for Cronulla. Transforming the iconic Kingsway, this development will create public engagement with the surrounding pedestrian streetscape. It will be a place that goes beyond premium homes, delivering a harmonious interplay between the built environment, individuals, and local communities. Beautifully positioned in the heart of Cronulla, Vue is a residential, retail and commercial precinct of coastal luxury. Having previously worked with Sammut Group, PBD Architects and Highland on multiple award-winning projects, our team at TOAST was brought onboard to craft the Place Vision, Place Thinking, Brand Footprint and Visual Identity of this destination. Founded on deep strategic research, immersing ourselves in the consumer market, insights and beliefs, and analysing market trends and competitors, our team understood that this place branding needed to be suave yet understated, showcasing its luxury lifestyle offering whilst seamlessly integrating into the locale. Solution: TOAST's passion is creating brands for places which become destinations for years to come. With a deep understanding of the marketing fundamentals of the property industry, we craft strategic brand platforms built for success. Sammut Group's Vue embodies the lure of understated luxury. Comprising designer apartments across 8-storeys, state-of-the-art facilities, and curated retail boutiques including one of Sydney's largest Harris Farm Markets, it is the intersection of splendour and contemporary convenience. A place where coastal luxury meets urban grandeur, it is a destination that is set to define Cronulla. The vision for this site was to create a lifestyle unlike anything ever seen before in Cronulla, a 'one-of-a-kind' interwoven expression of the best aspects of a coastal lifestyle harmoniously combined to create an iconic statement for the future. Building on this vision and the development's underplayed sophistication, our team crafted the Big Idea 'The Perfect Blend'; marrying luxe living with urban simplicity and seamlessly integrating resort-style amenities into contemporary dwellings, Vue is an interwoven expression of the best aspects of ocean view living, harmoniously combined with contemporary urban charm. This brand philosophy speaks true to Sammut Group's mission to deliver an elevated design vision achieving the perfect harmony between the building forms, the people, and the natural world of Cronulla. Mirroring PBD's architectural approach and Mim Design's interior visualisations, our designers worked closely with Sammut Group to craft Vue's brand identity as an amalgamation of attributes and cues inspired by its coastal location. The sense of expanse and perspective, the cultural connection and the ripple effect of the tides all combine to create landmark influences that radiate across the landscape, as reflected in Vue's name and timeless visual identity. The identity became a creative launchpad for amplification of a sophisticated suite of lead generation and sales support elements including a luxurious coffee table book, a brochure suite, digital and physical advertising campaign, website and digital-led display suite fit out, produced in close collaboration with sales agents Highland, PR team Left Field and marketers The Collective Co. A cornerstone of the creative campaign and marketing materials was sophisticated lifestyle photography and video content, directed and produced on location by TOAST. Showcasing the effortless luxury of coastal living, a two-day photoshoot captured a series of vignettes from yoga at dawn to cocktails at dusk with dozens of spontaneous moments enjoying salt, sea air and sun in between. Inspired by nature, infused with luxury, engineered for lifestyle; Vue is an elevated vision achieving the perfect blend of coastal and urban style, setting a new benchmark for coastal living.

Property.name: Highland Website
Property.tagline: We Are More Than Just Property
Property.description: Highland Website. Website Transformation. We Are More Than Just Property. In the hyper-competitive property and real estate market, breaking down all barriers to search, sell, rent or buy can be the difference between stagnation and success. With an attitude of dynamic innovation at its core and growth in its ambition, Highland approached TOAST with the challenge of genuinely raising the bar for how property services could be delivered. Challenge: On the back of two major digital transformation projects (our work for Juror and Caselaw) delivered for the NSW State Government, TOAST once again partnered with renowned UX/UI expert and published author Jerry Gaffney to transform and evolve the digital experience for real estate agency Highland. From residential to commercial sales, and property management to financial services, Highland offers it all. Our team's objective for the website transformation was to deliver these services in the most intuitive, compelling and customer-centric way possible.
